text:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Shrinagar House of Mangalsutra received two fold subscription on its first day of bidding led by huge response from employees.
The IPO aimed to raise Rs 400.95 crore with a fresh equity component with the price band fixed at Rs 155 to 165 per equity share, with a face value of Rs 10 each.
The IPO opened on 10 September and scheduled to close on 12 September followed by allotment on 15 September. Subsequently the IPO will be listed on the National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange on 17 September.
The grey market premium of Shrinagar House of Mangalsutra stood at Rs 30 at the time of filing this story which indicated the listing gain of 18 per cent, as per investorgain.
Choice Capital Advisors is the booking running lead manager for the IPO, whereas MUFG Intime is the registrar for the issue.
Subscription
On its first day of subscription, Shrinagar House of Mangalsutra IPO received a total subscription of 2 times led by retail investors and employees who subscribed the issue 2.84 times and 8.99 times respectively. Non-institutional buyers also showed a positive response towards the issue.
IPO Objectives
Shringar House of Mangalsutra plans to utilise the net proceeds from its upcoming IPO primarily to meet the company’s working capital requirements. The jewellery brand has earmarked Rs 280 crore towards funding working capital needs, ensuring smoother business operations and supporting future growth.
A portion of the funds will also be deployed for general corporate purposes, aimed at strengthening the company’s overall financial position and enhancing operational flexibility.
Company Earnings
Shringar House of Mangalsutra delivered strong growth in FY25, with revenue rising 30 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,430.12 crore, compared to Rs 1,102.71 crore in FY24. Profit after tax (PAT) nearly doubled, jumping 96 per cent to Rs 61.11 crore from Rs 31.11 crore in the previous fiscal.
The company’s EBITDA grew 82 per cent year-on-year to Rs 92.61 crore in FY25, reflecting improved operating efficiency. Assets expanded to Rs 375.75 crore, up from Rs 265 crore a year earlier, while net worth strengthened significantly to Rs 200.85 crore.
On the liabilities front, total borrowings stood at Rs 123.11 crore in FY25, rising from Rs 110.09 crore in FY24. Reserves and surplus were stable at Rs 123.72 crore.

text:

The data exceeded all projections in a Bloomberg survey of economists that had a 2.8% median estimate.

Higher production in export-oriented industries boosted manufacturing.
Malaysia’s central bank held borrowing costs last week amid low inflation and resilient consumption, after having cut the overnight policy rate by 25 basis points in July – its first such move in five years.
Bank Negara Malaysia governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said that the easing would boost economic growth for the rest of 2025 and into 2026.
“Still, the nation’s industrial production for the first seven months of 2025 grew at a slower pace of 2.4%, compared with 4% in the same period last year,” Uzir said.
Malaysia predicts economic growth of 4% to 4.8% this year, down from 5.1% in 2024, as it grapples with US president Donald Trump’s tariffs.

label: bastillepost.com;Australia highlights services trade at CIFTIS 2025 amid record global participation;https://www.bastillepost.com/global/article/5186181-australia-highlights-services-trade-at-ciftis-2025-amid-record-global-participation;2025-09-11T07:17:00+00:00
text:
Australia has stepped up its economic engagement with China, leading a record 59-company delegation to the China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing.
The 2025 CIFTIS opened in Beijing on Wednesday under the theme, "Embrace Intelligent Technologies, Empower Trade in Services."
As guest country of honor, Australia is spotlighting fast-growing sectors such as education, finance, and tourism. John Madew, Senior Trade and Investment Commissioner at the Australian Trade and Investment Commission (Austrade), said services are expanding faster than average and hold significant untapped potential in the China-Australia trade relationship.
"China is Australia's number one trading partner globally and has been for over 15 years. Last year it was about 310 billion dollars of two-way trade in goods and services. So that's really significant for Australia. And when you look at the trade, really, why is it so significant? We think it's the complementarity between our two economies, the clear mutual benefit that we both gain from the trading relationship and the people-to-people links that have been established between Australia and China that make it such a strong trading relationship," said Madew in an interview with China Global Television Network (CGTN).
He attributed the strength of the relationship to economic complementarity, mutual benefit, and deepening people-to-people ties.
"Services is a very important part of the trading relationship and one that's really growing faster than average. So we look at things like education, we look at things like financial services, tourism, as trade in services. So trade in services ends up at around 17 billion dollars annually. But as I said, lots of room to grow there," he said.
At this year's CIFTIS, a record number of agreements were signed between China and Australia. Among them were partnerships involving CPA Australia and the University of Adelaide, as well as technology company Canva, Australia's second unicorn, which is collaborating with Chinese schools.
Madew also expressed optimism about the role of CIFTIS in bringing together companies from service sectors in different countries.
"But I think the interesting thing to think about when we talk about these different agreements is this is the starting point, it's not the end point. So the great thing about something like CIFTIS is it's a platform for companies to start talking or make an agreement," He said.
CIFTIS 2025 is one of the world’s largest platforms for services trade, drawing nearly 2,000 exhibitors to Beijing. Among them are close to 500 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders including Walmart, AstraZeneca, and KPMG. Participants span 26 of the world’s top 30 countries and regions in services trade, underscoring the fair's growing international influence.

label: bastillepost.com;UN welcomes Iran-IAEA agreement: spokesperson;https://www.bastillepost.com/global/article/5186106-un-welcomes-iran-iaea-agreement-spokesperson;2025-09-11T06:22:00+00:00
text:
The United Nations welcomes the agreement reached between Iran and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) on the "practical modalities to resume inspections in Iran," said Stephane Dujarric, spokesperson for the UN secretary-general, on Wednesday.
Iran and the IAEA signed an agreement to resume cooperation on Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi announced in Egypt's capital Cairo during a joint press conference with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi.
"We welcome the agreement between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the IAEA on the 'practical modalities to resume inspections in Iran' as a positive step forward resuming full cooperation, as required by Iran's comprehensive safeguard agreement. label: wpenginepowered.com;Volvo CEO says every single new car will be electric by around 2035 as 'there's no turning back';https://scblondie.wpenginepowered.com/volvo-ceo-says-all-new-cars-electric-by-2035/;2025-09-11T06:00:00+00:00
text:
Volvo CEO Hakan Samuelsson has weighed in on the EU’s planned 2035 gas car ban, saying the industry’s future is fully electric and there is no turning back.
The Swedish automaker, owned by Geely, has already stopped making diesel cars and now sees gasoline engines facing their own expiration date.
While Volvo once pledged to sell only EVs by 2030, it has since softened the target to 90–100 percent of sales being plug-in hybrids and full EVs by decade’s end.
Even so, Samuelsson believes the market is clearly heading toward an electric-only reality.
SBX CARS – View live supercar auctions powered by Supercar Blondie
Volvo is going all-in on EVs and hybrids
In a recent interview with Bloomberg, the 74-year-old executive made his boldest prediction yet.
He said that the car industry will embrace EVs, and while it may take a bit longer in some region, the direction is clear.
“In (about) 10 years, cars will all be electric and they be lower cost,” he said.
It’s a striking statement considering Volvo’s electric sales are currently faltering.
Through the first eight months of 2025, Volvo sold just 90,326 EVs, down 24 percent from the same period last year, while plug-in hybrid sales dipped by one percent.
Gasoline models and mild hybrids also fell by seven percent, dragging the brand’s total deliveries down 10 percent to under 500,000 vehicles.
Still, the Volvo CEO insisted that the path forward is to strengthen plug-in hybrids, calling them ‘electric cars with a backup engine’, while building up the company’s EV lineup.
This includes the brand’s electric semi truck, which is crushing Tesla’s version in terms of deliveries made.
Volvo CEO believes those who don’t adapt may disappear
Samuelsson also warned that the coming electric era will spark industry-wide upheaval.
He predicts that by 2035, only a few global giants and ‘two or three very strong Chinese brands’ will dominate the landscape, while legacy players who fail to adapt may disappear.
This is in line with other experts, who also believe that only 15 of the 129 existing Chinese EV brands will survive by 2030.
That puts pressure not only on Volvo, but also on rivals like BMW, Mercedes, and Audi, many of whom are pushing back against the EU’s 2035 gas car ban.
In particular, Mercedes admitted that going all-in on EVs was a mistake, and is now rethinking their electric strategy.
Both Volvo and its sister brand Polestar are urging the EU to hold firm on its 2035 gas car ban, setting the stage for a showdown later this week when industry leaders meet to discuss the controversial ban.

label: fashionnetwork.com;John Lewis shrugs off wider losses as sales rise and customers are happier - FashionNetwork United Kingdom;https://uk.fashionnetwork.com/news/John-lewis-shrugs-off-wider-losses-as-sales-rise-and-customers-are-happier,1763078.html;2025-09-11T05:55:00+00:00
text:
John Lewis Partnership (JLP) is getting back on track its first-half results seemed to show on Thursday, as it appeared unperturbed by a wider loss that included a number of one-off items such as higher tax, investment costs and a packaging levy.
The six months to 26 July saw sales rising 4% to £6.2 billion as customer satisfaction reached a high and both the eponymous department stores and Waitrose supermarkets “outperformed their markets”.
Looking beyond the shock of much higher losses, its results statement did contain good news for the employee-owned company that just a few years ago seemed to be sabotaging its own operations by shedding experienced retail execs, looking for growth in areas wholly unconnected to retail and falling behind its peers in terms of tech and systems. That saw its previous good results being interrupted and staff (‘Partner’) bonuses being cancelled.
Ads But new management with a strong background in retail seems to be turning things around.
The company said its results show “positive momentum as a direct result of our customer focused investments”. Those investments are designed to drive long-term, sustainable growth and in the first half it accelerated its investment in store upgrades, digital services and essential modernisation to its technology and supply chain.
As mentioned, the result was that 4% increase in group sales while total revenue grew 5% to £5.4 billion. Its customer numbers also rose 4% and it saw “pleasing growth” in its loyalty schemes.
JLP’s loss before tax and exceptional items was £33 million, with the figure significantly impacted by one-off costs that it hadn't had to deal with a year earlier. On a like-for-like basis, that same loss was broadly flat compared to last year's £4 million deficit and was partly driven by heavy investment designed to drive long-term growth.
With exceptional items included, the loss before tax was £87 million with £54 million of exceptional items relating to its ongoing transformation and non-cash asset impairments. A year ago that loss had been £29 million.
The net loss was £62 million, wider than the £19 million deficit of H1 2024, with Partner bonuses, tax and exceptional items denting the latest figure to the tune of £29 million.
The company expects the majority of its sales and profit to come in the second half and said its investments have been helping to build momentum over the first half.
Looking at its individual operations, Waitrose supermarket sales rose 6% to £4.1 billion with a 3% rise in volumes. Adjusted operating profit was £110 million.
Meanwhile John Lewis sales rose 2% to £2.1 billion. The company said it has attracted more customers through its commitment to operating quality, style and value, “which has resonated strongly”. The retailer has been investing heavily in John Lewis with big initiatives in both fashion and beauty, adding new fashion labels for instance and upgrading beauty spaces.
It undertook a major refurbishment of its Liverpool store, added more omnichannel shopping options including 'deliver from store' and rapid online delivery and the recent return of its 100-year-old Never Knowingly Undersold promise “has continued to drive sales, relevance and value for money perceptions”.
It said: “ These investments and a renewed focus on compelling value, compounded by a sales mix shift towards Technology and Beauty, impacted gross margin in the short term.”
The adjusted operating loss was £53 million in the first half, down £4m, including incremental non-like-for-like taxation costs of £7 million from the new EPR packaging levy and incremental National Insurance Contributions.
It added that its first-half investment “allows us to look forward with confidence; our focus is now heading into peak where we see significant opportunity for all our core assortments”.
Chairman Jason Tarry said of all this: “Our clear focus on accelerating investment in our customers and our brands is working: more customers are shopping with us, driving sales, and helping Waitrose and John Lewis outperform their markets. We achieved our highest recorded levels of positive customer satisfaction.
“ The investments we are making, combined with our plans for peak trading, provide a strong foundation for the remainder of the year. While we are reporting a loss in the first half, we're well positioned to deliver full year profit growth, which we'll continue to invest in our customers and Partners.”

text:
Ghana’s Digital Leap: Unlocking $3.4 Billion in Potential by 2029
Imagine a Ghanaian farmer, previously reliant on fluctuating market prices and limited information, now accessing real-time data on crop demand and fair trade opportunities directly on their mobile phone. This isn’t a futuristic fantasy; it’s a rapidly approaching reality. A recent report by the GSMA estimates a staggering $3.4 billion in digital potential for Ghana by 2029, fueled by expanding mobile connectivity and innovative digital services. But what does this truly mean for businesses, consumers, and the nation’s economic future? This article dives deep into the key drivers, emerging trends, and actionable insights surrounding Ghana’s digital transformation.
The Expanding Digital Ecosystem: Key Drivers
The $3.4 billion figure isn’t simply a projection; it’s built on a foundation of significant growth in several key areas. Mobile penetration is rising steadily, driven by affordable smartphones and expanding 4G/5G networks. Crucially, the growth isn’t limited to urban centers. Increased infrastructure investment, particularly in rural areas, is bringing digital access to previously underserved populations. This expansion is coupled with a burgeoning fintech sector, offering mobile money solutions like MTN Mobile Money and Vodafone Cash, which are rapidly becoming the preferred method of financial transactions for many Ghanaians.
Did you know? Mobile money accounts now represent over 40% of all financial accounts in Ghana, demonstrating a significant shift in financial inclusion.
Mobile Money: The Engine of Digital Growth
The proliferation of mobile money is arguably the most significant driver of Ghana’s digital potential. It’s not just about convenience; it’s about unlocking economic opportunities for individuals and small businesses. Farmers can receive payments directly for their produce, reducing reliance on intermediaries. Small-scale traders can manage their finances more efficiently. And individuals can access financial services without the need for a traditional bank account. This is particularly impactful in a country where a large percentage of the population remains unbanked.
Bridging the Digital Divide: Infrastructure Investment
While mobile penetration is increasing, significant challenges remain in bridging the digital divide. Reliable internet access, particularly in rural areas, is still limited. Government initiatives, coupled with private sector investment, are crucial to expanding infrastructure and ensuring equitable access to digital services. The focus is shifting towards affordable data plans and community-based internet access points to reach those who are currently excluded.
Future Trends Shaping Ghana’s Digital Landscape
Looking ahead, several key trends are poised to accelerate Ghana’s digital transformation. These trends present both opportunities and challenges for stakeholders across the ecosystem.
The Rise of E-commerce and Digital Marketplaces
E-commerce is still in its nascent stages in Ghana, but it’s experiencing rapid growth. Platforms like Jumia and Tonaton are gaining traction, offering consumers access to a wider range of products and services. However, challenges remain in terms of logistics, trust, and payment security. The development of robust e-commerce infrastructure and consumer protection measures will be critical to unlocking the full potential of this sector.
Expert Insight: “The future of retail in Ghana is undoubtedly digital. However, success will depend on addressing the unique challenges of the local market, such as limited access to formal addresses and the prevalence of cash transactions.” – Dr. Ama Serwaa, Digital Economy Analyst.
The Impact of 5G and IoT
The rollout of 5G networks will be a game-changer for Ghana’s digital economy. Faster speeds and lower latency will enable a range of new applications, including smart agriculture, remote healthcare, and industrial automation. The Internet of Things (IoT) will play a key role in connecting devices and collecting data, providing valuable insights for businesses and governments.
Digital Skills Development: A Critical Imperative
Perhaps the most significant challenge facing Ghana’s digital transformation is the lack of skilled digital professionals. Investing in digital skills development is crucial to ensuring that Ghanaians can participate fully in the digital economy. This includes providing training in areas such as software development, data analytics, and digital marketing.
Pro Tip: Focus on developing skills that are in high demand, such as data science and cybersecurity, to maximize your career opportunities in the digital economy.
Actionable Insights for Businesses and Investors
Ghana’s digital potential presents a wealth of opportunities for businesses and investors. Here are some key areas to consider:
Fintech Innovation: Beyond Mobile Money
While mobile money is already a success story, there’s still significant room for innovation in the fintech sector. Opportunities exist in areas such as digital lending, insurance tech, and blockchain-based solutions.
AgriTech: Transforming the Agricultural Sector
Agriculture is a vital sector of the Ghanaian economy, but it’s often hampered by inefficiencies and lack of access to information. AgriTech solutions, such as precision farming, mobile-based extension services, and digital marketplaces, can help to improve productivity and profitability.
Healthcare Tech: Expanding Access to Care
Telemedicine and remote patient monitoring can help to expand access to healthcare services, particularly in rural areas. Digital health solutions can also improve the efficiency of healthcare delivery and reduce costs.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the biggest obstacle to Ghana’s digital transformation?
The biggest obstacle is the digital skills gap. Without a skilled workforce, Ghana will struggle to fully capitalize on its digital potential.
How can businesses benefit from Ghana’s digital growth?
Businesses can benefit by adopting digital technologies to improve efficiency, reach new customers, and develop innovative products and services.
What role does the government play in driving digital transformation?
The government plays a crucial role in creating a supportive regulatory environment, investing in infrastructure, and promoting digital literacy.
What is the expected impact of 5G on Ghana’s economy?
5G is expected to unlock new opportunities in areas such as smart agriculture, remote healthcare, and industrial automation, leading to significant economic growth.
Ghana’s digital journey is well underway, and the potential for growth is immense. By addressing the challenges and embracing the opportunities, Ghana can unlock its $3.4 billion digital future and create a more prosperous and inclusive economy for all. label: ariananews.af;Global partners strengthen Afghan Islamic finance sector;https://www.ariananews.af/global-partners-strengthen-afghan-islamic-finance-sector/;2025-09-11T06:58:00+00:00
text:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the Islamic Development Bank Institute (IsDBI), and the Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI) are scaling up efforts to strengthen Afghanistan’s financial sector through Islamic finance training and the adoption of international standards.
The partnership, part of the Global Islamic Finance and Impact Investing Platform (GIFIIP) launched by UNDP and IsDB in 2016, seeks to build resilience in Afghanistan’s fragile economy by positioning Islamic finance as a driver for sustainable development.
Since 2024, more than 120 officials from Da Afghanistan Bank, commercial banks, and microfinance institutions have received certifications in areas such as Shari’ah compliance, Islamic accounting, and financial reporting.
Training has included AAOIFI’s flagship programs—Certified Shari’ah Advisor & Auditor (CSAA), Certified Islamic Professional Accountant (CIPA), and others—alongside workshops on ethics, governance, and technical standards.
“These certifications are equipping Afghanistan’s financial sector with qualified professionals in Shari’ah compliance and financial reporting, ensuring alignment with global best practices,” the partners said in a joint statement.
By broadening institutional capacity and strengthening cross-border cooperation, the initiative aims to create a more inclusive financial system capable of supporting long-term growth.
Afghanistan’s banking sector has been under severe strain since the Islamic Emirate’s takeover in 2021, with international sanctions cutting off most external financing and foreign reserves.
Restrictions on the central bank have left commercial banks struggling with liquidity shortages, limited access to correspondent banking, and reduced public trust.
Within this constrained environment, Islamic finance is seen as a potential pathway to keep the sector functional, attract regional investment, and provide alternative tools for economic recovery.

While domestic factors are crucial, external elements, including fluctuating global commodity prices and geopolitical tensions, will play a role in shaping future trends. label: rbc.ua;US Congress passes $892B defense budget with Ukraine aid for 2026 | RBC-Ukraine;https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/congress-greenlights-2026-defense-bill-including-1757574956.html;2025-09-11T07:40:00+00:00
text:
Congress greenlights 2026 defense bill including $400M for Ukraine
Despite the opposition of part of the Republicans, the US House of Representatives supported the defense bill for 2026 with aid for Ukraine, according to The New York Times.
Yesterday, 10 September the House of Representatives adopted the bill on defense policy for the amount of 892.6 billion dollars, which provides for the increase of military readiness and the rise in salaries of American servicemen, at the same time prohibiting the provision to servicemen of medical assistance taking into account gender equality and rejecting efforts regarding the protection of access of servicemen to abortion services.
The bill was adopted by 231 votes against 196. The voting passed almost entirely along party lines. It showed how the Republicans turned the annual Pentagon defense document — which earlier was supported by both parties — into an instrument of advancing their conservative social ideas.
At the same time, despite the wave of opposition from Republicans to providing military aid to Ukraine, the defense policy bill provides for the allocation of 400 million dollars to the Pentagon’s initiative regarding assistance to Ukraine in the field of security.
The House of Representatives rejected the proposal of Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene, a Republican from the state of Georgia, to cut the financing of the country; at the same time, both Republicans and Democrats voted against.
In August, the United States approved new military aid to Ukraine for $203.5 million. RBC-Ukraine wrote about what the allocated funds will be directed to.
It is also worth noting that in recent days, Ukrainians named the countries that provided the most aid since the beginning of the war.

label: asiaone.com;'Robust' economic growth, higher consumer spending: Singapore collects nearly $89b in taxes, up 10.7%, Money News - AsiaOne;https://www.asiaone.com/money/robust-economic-growth-higher-consumer-spending-singapore-collects-nearly-89b-taxes-107;2025-09-11T07:35:00+00:00
text:
Singapore saw "robust" economic growth and higher consumer spending for the financial year (FY) 2024/25, with tax revenue reaching $89 billion.
This is 10.7 per cent higher than the $80.3 billion collected from April 2023 to March 2024, said the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) on Thursday (Sept 11).
The total tax revenue collected makes up about 76.9 per cent of the government's operating revenue and 12.2 per cent of Singapore's gross domestic product.
"The taxes collected play a vital role in supporting essential public services, driving economic growth, enhancing our living environment, and enabling social programmes that uplift the lives of Singaporeans," said IRAS.
The arrears rate for Goods and Services Tax (GST), income tax and property tax remained low at 0.66 per cent.
Arrears can be defined as being late or behind on overdue payments.
Corporate income tax largest contributor IRAS also said that although tax compliance remains high, it takes firm action against the "small minority of taxpayers who wilfully evade their tax obligations".
The authority audited and investigated over 8,600 cases in the last financial year, recovering about $507 million in taxes and penalties.
Corporate income tax, fuelled by strong corporate earnings, remained the largest contributor to tax revenue collection at 34.8 per cent.
It rose 6.7 per cent to $30.9 billion in FY2024, from $29 billion the previous financial year.
GST made up the second-largest share of tax revenue collection at 22.6 per cent, or $20 billion, up from $16.6 billion in the last financial year.
This increase reflects higher consumer spending and the adjustment in the GST rate from from eight to nine per cent stating Jan 1 last year, IRAS said.
Individual income tax accounted for the third-largest share of revenue collection at 21.5 per cent. It rose from $17.5 billion in FY2023 to $19.1 billion in FY2024.
This was driven by higher wages and an increase in the number of taxpayers, ccording to IRAS
Increase in stamp duty collection Property tax contributed 7.5 per cent ($6.6 billion) of the revenue collection, while stamp duty collection formed 7.4 per cent of revenue collection, also $6.6 billion.
The increase in stamp duty collection from $5.8 billion a year ago was largely attributed to a rise in property transaction volume.
In the last financial year, IRAS processed over $1.3 billion of disbursements to about 127,500 businesses, providing support for businesses, workers and jobs.
The grants were processed under various schemes, which included about $924 million under the progressive wage credit scheme, $277 million under the senior employment credit scheme and $51 million under the CPF transition offset.

text: Bond yields extended their upward trajectory in August, with the benchmark 10-year yield rising by 20 basis points (bps) and the longer end of the curve witnessing a sharper 30 bps increase.State Government Securities (SGS) saw an even steeper rise of nearly 50 bps, pushing yields in the 30-year and above segment to their highest levels in almost two years.“The pace and magnitude of the rise in long-term yields has been surprising,” said Puneet Pal, Head – Fixed Income, PGIM India Mutual Fund, attributing the surge to a demand-supply mismatch, fears of fiscal slippage, and expectations about the end of the rate-cutting cycle.Market sentiment turned negative after the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) maintained its policy stance while projecting Q1 FY27 inflation at 4.9%. This, despite the RBI lowering its FY26 average inflation forecast to 3.1% from 3.7%, led to a sell-off in bonds.CPI inflation dropped to 1.55% in August, largely due to easing food prices, while core inflation stayed steady at 4.1%. Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation remained in deflation at -0.58%, the lowest since August 2023. “In FY26 so far, WPI inflation has averaged 0.1%, sharply lower than 2.4% during the same period last year,” Pal noted.Adding to the macro narrative, S&P Global Ratings upgraded India’s sovereign rating to BBB from BBB- with a stable outlook, citing political stability and strong infrastructure spending. This marks the first upgrade since 2007.S&P expects India’s combined fiscal deficit to narrow to 6.6% by 2028 from 7.3% currently, and sees the debt-to-GDP ratio reducing to 78.5% from 82.4%. Fitch, however, retained its rating at BBB-.The government’s plans to rationalise GST slabs to spur consumption and offset U.S. tariff impacts have raised fiscal concerns. Initial estimates suggest a cost of 0.3–0.4% of GDP annually. “This GST rationalisation has added to the upward move in bond yields, even though the S&P rating upgrade initially cheered markets,” said Pal.On growth, real GDP for Q1 FY26 printed at 7.8%, ahead of expectations, though nominal GDP slowed to 8.8% due to a weak deflator. Stronger real growth was supported by lower input price pressures, higher government spending, and front-loaded exports. “While GDP growth may moderate, we don’t see material downside risks to the RBI’s FY26 projection of 6.5%,” Pal observed, adding that the bar for further rate cuts remains high.Meanwhile, robust rainfall and higher sowing activity supported the agricultural outlook. On the fiscal front, the Centre’s deficit reached 30% of the FY26 target by July, driven by weak tax revenues and strong expenditure, while states clocked 22% of their budgeted deficit. Bond markets remain wary of slippages, though Pal expects the government to manage revenue shortfalls through expenditure rationalisation.India’s current account deficit narrowed sharply to $2.4 billion (0.2% of GDP) in Q1 FY26, the lowest first-quarter print since 2017. However, the rupee weakened by 1% in August, making it one of the worst-performing EM currencies, partly due to U.S. tariffs. FPIs pulled out funds from equities, though debt flows remained positive at $1.8 billion.Looking ahead, Pal believes the steep rise in yields has opened opportunities for investors. “Bond valuations have become attractive, especially at the longer end and in the SDL space. We expect the RBI to take steps to address the dislocation, particularly in SDLs,” he said. Over the next few months, he sees the 10-year benchmark trading in the 6.30–6.70% range, with SDLs expected to outperform over the medium term.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. text:
In a big cheer for Provident Fund or PF subscribers, the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) may roll out features like withdrawals from ATMs and ban-like transactions ahead of Diwali.
Tired of too many ads? go ad free now The meeting, to be chaired by labour and employment minister Mansukh Mandaviya, is scheduled for October 10-11, although the final agenda remains pending, sources informed ET. The government intends to introduce certain advantages for approximately 80 million EPFO subscribers before Diwali to enhance spending patterns. New EPFO features soon The EPFO may consider the EPFO 3.0 initiative at its meeting next month, aiming to introduce facilities similar to banking services, including options for withdrawing a portion of provident funds via ATMs or using them for UPI transactions.
The organisation's central board of trustees is also expected to review a proposal to increase the minimum pension from Rs 1,000 monthly to between Rs 1,500 and Rs 2,500, addressing a persistent request from trade unions. EPFO: Safety cover The apex decision-making authority of EPFO, the Central Board of Trustees, comprises members representing employers, employees, state governments and the central government. The suggestion to enable partial withdrawals via banks and UPI might encounter opposition from trade unions, who consistently maintain that provident funds are meant for retirement security.
Trade unions express concern that allowing withdrawals through banking channels could undermine the fundamental purpose of these savings, particularly if used for purposes beyond those currently permitted by regulations, according to the ET report. The Employees' Provident Fund & Miscellaneous Provisions Act currently permits automated withdrawals of up to Rs 5 lakh for specific needs such as health emergencies, educational expenses, matrimonial purposes and housing requirements, with processing completed within three days without manual intervention.
Tired of too many ads? go ad free now The existing withdrawal system requires a minimum of two to three days for processing and relies on NEFT or RTGS transfers. text:
The settlement results in SpiceJet gaining $79.6 million in cash reserves for aircraft and engine maintenance, and $9.9 million in credits
Indian low-cost carrier SpiceJet announced a crucial liquidity boost on Thursday, leading to a 5.3% gain in the stock price.
Add Asianet Newsable as a Preferred Source
SpiceJet announced the finalization of a settlement with Carlyle Aviation Partners, gaining $79.6 million in cash reserves for aircraft and engine maintenance, and $9.9 million in credits to reduce its lease payments.
This deal strengthens the airline’s ongoing restructuring efforts and provides a much-needed breather for the debt-laden airline.
SpiceJet Restructuring
As part of the broader agreement, Carlyle Aviation Partners and its affiliates will restructure certain lease obligations worth $121.18 million. In addition, SpiceJet will issue equity shares worth $50 million to the lessors.
The settlement also includes a mechanism where, if the lessors realize proceeds above $50 million from the sale of these shares, part of the surplus will be used to offset future lease obligations.
Additionally, the promoter or its nominated assignee will have the right to buy these equity shares once the statutory lock-in period ends.
“This agreement marks a significant milestone in our ongoing restructuring and un‐grounding efforts. The support extended by Carlyle demonstrates their confidence in SpiceJet’s long‐term prospects. This transaction meaningfully reduces our liabilities, strengthens our balance sheet, and positions us well for sustainable growth,” said Ajay Singh, Chairman & Managing Director, SpiceJet.
This comes after SpiceJet completed the full payment of $24 million to Credit Suisse earlier this month.
As of March 2025, the airline company had a debt of ₹4,218.51 crore.
Weak Q1 Print
Last week, SpiceJet reported a 42.3% decline in Q1 consolidated total income to ₹12.01 billion, and posted a loss of ₹2.34 billion, compared to a profit of ₹1.58 billion in the same period last year.
Year-to-date, the stock has sunk over 40%.

label: devdiscourse.com;Nuclear watchdog chief announces breakthrough on Iran monitoring | Headlines;https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/headlines/3623015-nuclear-watchdog-chief-announces-breakthrough-on-iran-monitoring;2025-09-11T07:46:00+00:00
text: At the time, the Iranian authorities confirmed that the Natanz enrichment site had been “impacted” without affecting existing radiation levels, the top IAEA diplomat said. The head of the UN’s atomic energy agency announced on Wednesday that a deal has been struck with Iran to resume cooperation on inspections of Tehran’s nuclear facilities. “Indispensable” monitoring by the International Atomic Energy Agency ( IAEA ) ended in June, agency chief Rafael Grossi said, when Israel and US-backed airstrikes targeted Iran’s nuclear power installations. At the time, the Iranian authorities confirmed that the Natanz enrichment site had been “impacted” without affecting existing radiation levels, the top IAEA diplomat said. Now, “practical modalities” have been agreed to allow the resumption of inspection activities in Iran, Mr. Grossi told the agency’s board of governors in the Austrian capital. “This is an important step in the right direction,” he continued, before expressing his gratitude to Egypt for brokering the deal. The development follows the 28 August announcement by France, Germany and the UK of their intention to reimpose UN sanctions on Iran within 30 days, under the so-called “snapback” mechanism contained in the Iranian nuclear agreement signed in July 2015 by the five permanent members of the UN Security Council , in addition to Germany, the EU and Iran. The new agreement – which was preceded by weeks of technical discussions in Tehran and Vienna over verification activities of “all facilities and installations in Iran”– came despite the decision by Iranian lawmakers on 25 June to suspend cooperation with IAEA, a move approved by the country’s President one week later. At the time, Mr. Grossi noted that this domestic decision did not alter Iran’s international nuclear non-proliferation treaty (NPT) obligations . And earlier this week, he insisted that the NPT agreement remained in force as “the sole legally binding treaty governing the rights and obligations of the [IAEA] and Iran with respect to safeguards implementation in Iran”. While acknowledging that his Iranian interlocutors had declared their willingness to remain part of the international non-proliferation movement, Mr. Grossi noted Tehran’s “concerns”. Nonetheless, the deal – sealed by Mr. Grossi and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi in Cairo on Monday – “provides for a clear understanding of the procedures for inspection, notifications and their implementation”, he insisted. The agreement also “contemplates” reporting on all facilities targeted by Israel and the US in June “including the nuclear material present” in Iran, the IAEA chief continued. “These practical steps…need to be implemented now,” he insisted. “There may be difficulties and issues to be resolved for sure, but we now know what we have to do and the elements at our disposal for these basic understandings to be implemented.” Visit UN News for more.

Shakeout Signals: Bitcoin Poised for a Surge Beyond $130,000
As the cryptocurrency market continues to evolve, Bitcoin remains the bedrock of the digital assets world, often setting the tone for the entire sector. In recent weeks, signals in the market suggest that Bitcoin may be on the brink of an upward surge, potentially exceeding the $130,000 mark. This article delves into the underlying factors, market shakeout signals, and what investors should keep in mind as these developments unfold.
Understanding Shakeout Signals
In trading terminology, a “shakeout” occurs when a market experiences a temporary downturn, leading to a rapid and often emotional sell-off. This can create a false impression of a bearish trend, tricking inexperienced traders into exiting their positions just before a significant price increase. Many seasoned investors capitalize on this volatility, viewing it as an opportunity to accumulate more assets at lower prices.
Currently, specific indicators in Bitcoin’s price chart reveal shakeout signals that suggest we might be at a pivotal moment. Historically, Bitcoin has demonstrated impressive resilience following such shakeouts, often building enough momentum to reach new all-time highs.
Factors Fueling the Speculation
-
Institutional Adoption: In recent months, institutional interest in Bitcoin has surged. From major corporations to hedge funds, more entities are recognizing Bitcoin’s potential as a store of value and an inflation hedge. This institutional buying pressure lays the groundwork for sustained price increases.
-
Scarcity and Halving Events: Bitcoin’s protocol dictates that the total supply is capped at 21 million coins, with mining rewards halving approximately every four years. The next halving event is projected for 2024, reducing the rate at which new Bitcoin is introduced into circulation. This built-in scarcity often leads to price increases post-halving as demand continues to outstrip supply.
-
Macroeconomic Influences: Central banks worldwide are resorting to extraordinary monetary policies to combat inflation, often resulting in diminished confidence in fiat currencies. As Bitcoin is increasingly viewed as “digital gold,” its appeal grows as a hedge against economic uncertainty.
-
Technological Advances and Network Upgrades: The ongoing development of the Bitcoin network, including the implementation of scaling solutions like the Lightning Network, enhances Bitcoin’s utility as a medium of exchange. Improved transaction speeds and lower fees can drive user adoption, further boosting demand.
-
Retail Investor Sentiment: Trends in retail investor behavior are showing signs of increasing confidence in Bitcoin. Social media sentiment, trading volumes, and activity on platforms like Coinbase and Binance suggest that more retail investors are re-entering the market, which can contribute to upward price momentum.
Technical Analysis: Key Levels to Watch
Technical analysis plays a crucial role in predicting Bitcoin’s potential price movements. Key resistance levels lie just below the $130,000 mark, where past sell-offs have occurred. A sustained breakout above this level, supported by strong trading volumes, would signal a bullish trend.
Additionally, other indicators, such as the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and Moving Averages, provide insights into overbought or oversold conditions, helping traders make educated decisions.
Cautionary Notes for Investors
While the indications for a potential Bitcoin surge are compelling, investors must exercise caution. Volatility is synonymous with cryptocurrency markets, and prices can swing dramatically in either direction. It is essential for investors to conduct thorough research, set realistic expectations, and never invest more than they can afford to lose.
Conclusion
The current shakeout signals intertwined with institutional adoption, macroeconomic trends, and technological advancements suggest that Bitcoin could indeed be on the verge of a significant price surge. As the market anticipates the potential for Bitcoin to surpass the $130,000 threshold, investors are encouraged to remain vigilant and informed. While the future of Bitcoin holds great promise, strategic decision-making in the face of volatility is key to capitalizing on this emerging opportunity. The cryptocurrency landscape will continue to unfold, and with it, the possibility of unprecedented growth for Bitcoin remains very much alive.

label: marketscreener.com;On Wall Street, Oracle Shatters Expectations | MarketScreener;https://www.marketscreener.com/news/on-wall-street-oracle-shatters-expectations-ce7d59dcdf81f02c;2025-09-10T06:19:00+00:00
text: Markets remain buoyed by expectations of a rate cut from the Federal Reserve, widely anticipated at next week’s policy meeting. Yesterday’s sharply downward revision to US job creation figures—part of a routine labour market data update—only reinforced this scenario. Today’s PPI data and tomorrow’s August inflation print are now eagerly awaited to confirm, or perhaps even extend, the narrative. Unlike the relatively muted start to the week, however, the newsflow is now considerably denser. On the geopolitical front, Donald Trump and Narendra Modi have agreed to fast-track talks aimed at resolving the escalating trade tensions between their countries. The US currently levies a 50% tariff on most Indian imports. In Europe, tensions flared after Poland was forced to temporarily shut down Warsaw airport to intercept Russian drones that had violated its airspace during an attack on western Ukraine. Meanwhile, in the Middle East, Washington expressed dismay over an Israeli strike targeting Hamas officials in Qatar—a close US ally. In macroeconomic developments, Lisa Cook may prove harder to “cook” than expected—if you'll pardon the polyglot culinary pun. A federal judge has temporarily blocked her dismissal from the Federal Reserve Board by President Trump, arguing that the fraud allegations put forward are not yet sufficient grounds for removal. It’s a modest victory for the Powell camp at the Fed, which remains locked in a fierce battle against the Trump administration’s creeping encroachment on the institution’s independence. In corporate news, US tech reasserted its dominance yesterday. Apple held its customary autumn event to unveil new products, most notably the iPhone 17. Reviewers showed particular enthusiasm for the iPhone 17 Air, a sleek and ultra-thin model. However, the company continues to lag when it comes to AI. While analysts were impressed, investors were less so: Apple shares dropped 1.5% after the presentation, signalling a lukewarm reception, primarily due to its ongoing AI shortcomings. Oracle , on the other hand, appears to have no such troubles. Arguably the day’s headline story on Wall Street, the software behemoth stunned the market with its quarterly earnings release. For the uninitiated, Oracle is something of a tech dinosaur, founded in 1977—a year after Apple and two years after Microsoft. A far cry from TikTok and OpenAI. With a current valuation of $680 billion, Oracle ranks as the 12th largest US company. But when markets open at 3:30pm UK time, that figure could climb to around $860 billion, propelling it into the top 10 and leapfrogging both Walmart and JPMorgan. That’s because the stock surged 28% in after-hours trading following its Q1 fiscal results (Oracle’s somewhat eccentric fiscal year begins on June 1, for the accounting enthusiasts among you). Why such euphoria? The company revealed a staggering surge in its order backlog, providing unprecedented forward visibility. And when I say staggering, I mean it: up 360%, reaching $455 billion in orders (yes, that’s billion with a “b”). The cherry on top? This explosive growth—largely unanticipated by analysts—is driven in part by cloud server rentals, with related revenues expected to soar from $10 billion in 2025 to over $140 billion by 2030. You guessed it: all thanks to AI applications. Oracle has clearly ticked both the hypergrowth and AI boxes this past quarter—hence the market’s spectacular reaction. Given Oracle’s size, one can easily imagine the ripple effects across Wall Street indices. The news also re-energises the narrative around the long-term viability of AI investments. To quote sector specialist Martin Peers of The Information , it demonstrates just how profoundly AI-related contracts can reshape a business—even one previously considered a second-tier player in the cloud arena. Alongside what promises to be a buoyant US market open, today’s main event is the swearing-in of Emmanuel Macron’s latest “disposable” Prime Minister, Sébastien Lecornu, and the release of US Producer Price Index data at 2:30pm UK time. In the Asia-Pacific region, the mood was equally upbeat. Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.8%, India’s NIFTY rose 0.5%, and Australia’s ASX added 0.4%. Gains were even stronger in Hong Kong (+1%), Taiwan (+1.4%), and South Korea, where the KOSPI rallied 2% on the back of Oracle’s results and rumours of local stock market reform. European futures suggest a broadly positive open. On the agenda today: the CPI in China; in the United States, the final demand of the PPI, wholesale inventories, and DOE crude oil inventories. > ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 11 — Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said today he is confident the state can achieve a projected revenue of RM2.5 billion this year.
He added that Johor is on track to record its highest revenue in history, citing ongoing development plans, including contributions from the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
“I have also detailed the performance of the state's revenue in the past 10 years, where from 2015 to 2021, Johor's state revenue was around RM1.5 billion to RM1.7 billion.

"However, we cannot deny that this drastic increase in state revenue is due to contributions through the JS-SEZ.

7 Shocking Index Funds Quietly Outperforming the Market
The Ultimate List of Market-Crushing Index Funds
For decades, the S&P 500 has reigned as the undisputed champion of passive investing, offering a simple, low-cost path to broad market exposure. Yet, in an era of rapid innovation and shifting market dynamics, a new class of index funds has emerged from the shadows. These are not your average, cap-weighted behemoths; they are specialized, rules-based funds designed to capitalize on specific market trends and inefficiencies. The following list highlights a selection of funds that have consistently delivered market-beating returns, proving that sometimes, the best investment opportunities are found just outside the mainstream.
- Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF (SPMO): Riding the wave of top-performing stocks with a rules-based strategy that has delivered a 49% return in 2024.
- Global X Uranium ETF (URA): A high-risk, high-reward thematic play on nuclear energy, with a one-year return exceeding 71%.
- Invesco S&P SmallCap 600 Pure Value ETF (RZV): A strategic value-based approach that has proven its worth by focusing on undervalued small-cap companies.
- VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO): A concentrated bet on digital entertainment megatrends that posted a 47.6% return in 2024.
- Vanguard Growth ETF (VUG): From a low-cost giant, a fund that has generated a 10-year compound annual return of 16.2%, comfortably beating the S&P 500’s 12.8% over the same period.
- Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF (MGK): An even more concentrated play on mega-cap tech, with a blistering 17% annual growth rate over the last decade.
- Pacer American Energy Independence ETF (USAI): A specialized energy fund with a strong risk-adjusted return (Sharpe ratio of 2.87) and a total return of 44% in 2024.
The Secret to Outperformance: Beyond the S&P 500
The exceptional performance of these funds is not an accident; it is the result of a fundamental departure from the traditional index fund model. To understand why these funds have succeeded, it is first necessary to grasp how they differ from the most common benchmark and what alternative strategies they employ.
A. The “Index” You Know vs. the Index You Need to Know
Most of the major indexes that investors are familiar with, such as the S&P 500, are weighted by market capitalization. This means the largest companies in the index have the largest influence on its performance. While this model has long been a cornerstone of passive investing, it has led to a significant and often overlooked issue. The S&P 500, traditionally a bellwether for the American economy and its 500 largest companies, is no longer a truly broad-based index.
The index has become a de facto concentrated growth fund, with a disproportionate amount of its performance and risk tied to a handful of mega-cap technology stocks. A recent analysis indicates that the top 10 companies in the S&P 500 now account for a staggering 38% of the index’s total weight and contribute to an even more shocking 53% of its risk, as measured by standard deviation. This concentration is not merely a data point; it represents a fundamental shift in market dynamics. As the valuations of a few tech giants swell, their influence on the cap-weighted index becomes enormous, amplifying both upside and downside risk for the entire index. This phenomenon provides a compelling rationale for investors to seek alternative strategies to achieve true diversification and potentially superior returns.
B. The Rise of “Strategic Beta” and Factor-Based Investing
The funds on the preceding list are not traditional index funds. Instead, they are often classified as “strategic beta” or “factor-based” funds. This investment style represents a powerful blend of passive and active management. While they passively follow a rules-based index, the rules themselves are actively designed to capture specific market inefficiencies or “factors,” such as momentum, value, or low volatility.
A momentum strategy, for example, is based on the principle that securities that have performed well recently will continue to do so for a period of time. The Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF (SPMO) is a prime example of this methodology. It tracks the 100 stocks from the S&P 500 that have demonstrated the highest recent price performance, adjusting for volatility and then weighting the portfolio based on a combination of company size and momentum score.
Other strategic beta funds address market inefficiencies by focusing on value or equal-weighting. A value strategy, as exemplified by the Invesco S&P SmallCap 600 Pure Value ETF (RZV), aims to identify and invest in companies that are considered undervalued based on fundamental metrics like price-to-earnings ratios, price-to-book ratios, or dividends. The equal-weighting strategy, in contrast, gives every stock in a given index the same weighting, effectively neutralizing the concentration risk inherent in market-cap-weighted indices.
C. Thematic Investing: A Concentrated Bet on Megatrends
Another powerful strategy for generating outsized returns is thematic investing. These funds focus on a specific sector, industry, or global trend, such as technology, energy, or consumer goods. This approach is not about tracking a broad market; it is a concentrated bet on a macro-level shift.
Thematic investing is a double-edged sword. On one hand, it can generate explosive returns by capitalizing on favorable trends, as seen with the Global X Uranium ETF (URA), which has returned over 219% over the last three years, or the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO), which gained 47.6% in 2024. On the other hand, the concentrated nature of these funds makes them inherently high-risk and volatile. This is demonstrated by the significant losses suffered by other specialized funds, such as the Quant Teck Fund, which lost 13.57% in 2025. The causal relationship is clear: the same lack of diversification that allows for amplified gains in a bull market for a specific sector also exposes the investor to outsized losses when that sector faces a downturn or unfavorable market conditions. This critical duality must be understood before investing in these high-stakes vehicles.
A Closer Look at Our Top Picks
To fully appreciate the potential and risk of these funds, it is essential to move beyond surface-level descriptions and examine their specific mechanics and performance history. The following table and fund profiles provide a detailed look at the selected funds.

A. Fund Profiles
The Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF (SPMO) leverages a sophisticated, rules-based methodology to identify and invest in the 100 stocks from the S&P 500 that have demonstrated the strongest recent price performance. This strategy has paid off handsomely, with the fund up over 49% year to date through December 17, largely due to its concentrated holdings in the dominant technology sector. Its top holdings include NVIDIA, Meta Platforms, and Amazon, demonstrating how a factor-based fund’s performance can be directly tied to the success of a few key stocks.
The Global X Uranium ETF (URA) is a compelling case study in pure thematic investing. As its name suggests, it is a focused bet on the global uranium and nuclear energy sector. Its portfolio is extremely concentrated, with its top 10 holdings accounting for 68.16% of its total assets. The fund’s impressive 71.74% one-year return highlights its high-growth potential, which is a direct consequence of the speculative and highly specialized nature of its underlying assets.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO) offers investors a way to gain exposure to the rapidly expanding global video gaming and eSports industry. The fund’s 47.6% total return in 2024 demonstrates its ability to capitalize on this megatrend. However, the fund’s price history also serves as a clear indicator of the volatility inherent in such specialized investments, with its 52-week price range spanning from $116.00 to $68.05.
The Vanguard Growth ETF (VUG) and Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF (MGK) are fascinating examples of how a fund’s label can be misleading. While they carry the Vanguard brand name, a titan of low-cost, diversified indexing, these funds are in practice highly concentrated growth plays. Their market-beating returns over the last decade are not a product of broad diversification but rather a direct result of their extreme concentration in a handful of technology giants. The Vanguard Growth ETF’s top five holdings represent 44.2% of its total portfolio, while the Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF’s top five holdings are a staggering 50.3%. The outsized influence of these stocks is the direct cause of the funds’ exceptional performance, particularly given that a high proportion of their holdings have delivered a median return of 833% over the past decade. This demonstrates that the “index fund” label does not always guarantee the broad diversification that investors might assume.
The Hidden Risks of Chasing Returns
While the lure of market-beating returns is strong, a thorough analysis requires a balanced perspective. The very attributes that enable these specialized funds to outperform the market also expose investors to significant, and often hidden, risks.
A. Concentration Risk: The Double-Edged Sword
As demonstrated by the Vanguard funds, the high degree of concentration in a few stocks or a single sector is the primary driver of outsized returns. However, this is a double-edged sword. This same concentration makes these funds susceptible to disproportionate losses if a single stock or sector underperforms. For example, a major data breach, a regulatory crackdown, or a product failure at a top-weighted company could significantly harm the fund’s performance. The Invesco QQQ Trust, a fund with a similar high-concentration strategy to the Vanguard funds, provides a historical illustration of this risk, having fallen more than 40% during the 2008 financial crisis.
B. The Illiquidity Trap
For a novice investor, a fund’s liquidity might seem like a minor detail, but it is a critical measure of risk. The liquidity of an ETF is determined by both its secondary market trading volume and the liquidity of its underlying assets. Many niche or specialized ETFs, particularly those with a lower total asset under management (AUM) or those that invest in less-liquid securities, may face an illiquidity trap. This can lead to wider bid-ask spreads, which are the difference between the highest price a buyer is willing to pay and the lowest price a seller is willing to accept. This hidden transaction cost can significantly erode an investor’s returns, even in a fund with a low expense ratio, and can make it difficult and costly to exit a position at a fair price during times of market stress.
C. Understanding Volatility
These specialized funds are often significantly more volatile than a broad-market index. While a diversified fund like a total stock market index may experience a general market downturn, a thematic or factor-based fund can suffer from sector-specific declines that are far more severe. The fund’s risk profile is a direct reflection of its investment objective and the assets it holds to meet that objective. For investors with a lower risk tolerance or a shorter time horizon, this elevated volatility can lead to substantial losses and a greater risk of capital erosion.
How to Research and Invest in Niche Funds
For investors who are willing to accept the increased risks for the potential of higher returns, a strategic and disciplined approach to research is essential. Investing in these specialized vehicles requires a deeper level of due diligence than simply buying a traditional, broad-based index fund.
A. Essential Research Tools and Metrics
Before committing capital, a prospective investor should adopt a rigorous research process, guided by the E-E-A-T principle (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness). This framework ensures that all information is accurate, verifiable, and from a credible source. A checklist of key metrics is crucial for evaluating a fund’s true value proposition and its risks. These metrics include:
- Expense Ratio: The ongoing management fee, typically expressed as a percentage of the fund’s net asset value (NAV).
- Total Assets Under Management (AUM): A key indicator of a fund’s stability and liquidity. Larger funds often have more liquid underlying assets and smaller bid-ask spreads.
- Trading Volume and Bid-Ask Spread: Critical for assessing transaction costs. A high average daily volume and a tight bid-ask spread generally indicate greater liquidity and lower trading costs.
- Tracking Error: The measure of how closely a fund’s performance aligns with its underlying index. A low tracking error indicates that the fund is effectively replicating its benchmark, minimizing the risk of a performance shortfall.
B. Where to Look
Authoritative and reliable resources are essential for conducting proper due diligence. Tools like the FINRA Fund Analyzer and Fidelity’s ETF Evaluator provide investors with the ability to search, compare, and analyze thousands of funds based on a variety of criteria, including performance, fees, holdings, and volatility. Utilizing such platforms allows for a direct, side-by-side comparison of different funds, empowering investors to make decisions based on verifiable data rather than speculation.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Q: What is the difference between an ETF and a mutual fund?
Both ETFs and mutual funds are pooled investment vehicles, but they differ in how they are traded and priced. Mutual funds are typically priced once per day, and all orders are executed at the end-of-day price. In contrast, an ETF trades like a stock on a major exchange throughout the day, experiencing price fluctuations just like any publicly traded company.
Q: Are these funds riskier than a standard S&P 500 index fund?
Yes, in most cases, these specialized funds are considered to be riskier. While broad-based indices offer diversification across a wide range of companies and sectors, many of the funds highlighted here are highly concentrated in a specific industry, country, or investment style. This concentration, while a driver of higher returns, also exposes investors to a greater risk of loss if that specific area of the market underperforms.
Q: Why do some funds have a higher expense ratio?
Many specialized ETFs, including strategic beta and thematic funds, have higher expense ratios than their traditional index fund counterparts. This is because their rules-based or actively managed approach may require more frequent rebalancing or sophisticated analysis, leading to higher operational costs. Additionally, funds with a smaller AUM may have a higher expense ratio to cover their fixed operational costs.
Q: How much money do I need to get started?
The amount of money needed to start investing in ETFs is generally low. Many online brokers and trading platforms have no account minimums, and some offer the ability to set up regular investment plans with as little as 1 AED per month. This makes ETF investing accessible to a wide range of investors, regardless of their starting capital.

Positive Points Old Mutual Ltd ( FRA:2KS ) reported a strong earnings story with a 19% growth in RFO per share and a 31% increase in adjusted headline earnings per share.

The company achieved a 9% growth in its dividend to ZAR0.37 per share, supported by strong equity market performance.
Old Mutual Ltd ( FRA:2KS ) received an improved MSCI rating from AA to AAA, recognizing its commitment to sustainability.
Negative Points The group's value of new business margin decreased to 1.3%, primarily due to assumption and model changes in the South Africa Life and Savings business.
Persistency pressure in the Mass and Foundation cluster negatively impacted financial results, leading to a decline in the group's embedded value.
The regulatory solvency ratio decreased from 180% to 170%, partly due to increased market shocks and dividend accruals.
Old Mutual Ltd ( FRA:2KS ) faces challenges in its growth markets, particularly in East Africa, West Africa, and China, requiring a turnaround in margins and returns.
The company reported a significant restructuring provision of ZAR440 million, indicating ongoing efforts to manage costs and improve efficiency.

Q : How does Old Mutual plan to measure expenses and efficiency? Q : Can you provide a breakdown of the ZAR1.7 billion economic variances in life embedded value? A : Nico van der Colff, OML Group Actuary, indicated that the IFRS investment information can be used as a proxy for shareholder investment returns. The embedded value was affected by method changes, and the variances are based on opening assumptions, which already accounted for weaker persistency in the Mass and Foundation cluster.
Q : What structural changes in the market are affecting persistency? A : Jurie Strydom, CEO, noted increased competition in the funeral market and macroeconomic headwinds in South Africa. There is a blurring of lines between banks and insurance companies, leading to higher churn in funeral business. Management actions are in place to improve persistency, but structural changes are recognized.
Q : What are the biggest opportunities for cost reduction across the group? A : Casparus Troskie, CFO, highlighted that cost reductions are targeted in central functions, aiming to return to 2022 cost levels plus inflation. The new operating model and a leaner center function present further opportunities for cost savings.

label: riotimesonline.com;Brazil's Ibovespa Climbs on Inflation Relief Faces Trade;https://www.riotimesonline.com/brazils-ibovespa-climbs-on-inflation-relief-faces-trade-hurdles/;2025-09-11T06:49:00+00:00
text:
B3 data shows the Ibovespa index rose 0.54 percent to 142,386.85 points on September 10. Traders lifted the benchmark, led by Petrobras shares. The energy giant advanced amid stable global oil prices.
IBGE data confirms the IPCA inflation fell 0.11 percent in August. This beat estimates of -0.15 percent and held the 12-month rate at 5.13 percent. Businesses gain from reduced costs that support growth plans.
The index touched 143,181.59 points at its peak that day. It approached the record of 143,408.64 from September 5. A low of 141,611.77 points marked initial caution.
Top gainers included C&A Modas (CEAB3) up 4.80 percent. Retail stocks surged on lower inflation that aids consumer spending. Marfrig (MRFG3) climbed 4.17 percent, as a weaker real boosted exporter profits.
Magazine Luiza (MGLU3) gained 3.70 percent in e-commerce. Banco do Brasil (BBAS3) rose about 2.5 percent on banking optimism. Petrobras (PETR4) added roughly 1.8 percent from energy demand.
Volumes hit 16.76 billion reais, under the yearly average of 23.7 billion. Traders stayed reserved, with September’s average at 18.2 billion. This low turnover reflects merchant wariness over risks.
The dollar dropped 0.54 percent to 5.40 reais. This helps agribusiness firms like Marfrig in foreign sales. It eases import bills for local buyers.
Brazilian Stocks Struggle as U.S. Rate Bets Meet Tariff Pressures
U.S. Labor Department reports producer prices eased 0.1 percent in August. Services fell 0.2 percent, goods up 0.1 percent. The yearly rise slowed to 2.6 percent from 3.1 percent.
This data raises chances of a 0.25 point Federal Reserve cut soon. Lower U.S. rates pull capital to Brazil’s market. Merchants here seek those funds for trades.
Yet political issues cast doubt. The Supreme Court restarted Jair Bolsonaro’s trial on September 10. Investors ignore the outcome but watch for U.S. reactions.
Trump set 50 percent tariffs on Brazilian items in July. He tied them to the trial, affecting steel and farm exports. Traders prepare for profit squeezes.
Top losers featured MRV Engenharia (MRVE3) down 4.83 percent. Real estate suffers from sticky high rates despite inflation drop. Raizen (RAIZ4) fell 4.44 percent in biofuels.
Braskem (BRKM5) declined amid chemical sector pressures. Brava Energia (BRAV3) lost about 1.66 percent on oil swings. WEG (WEGE3) dipped 1.59 percent in industrials.
The daily chart keeps an uptrend channel from August. The 50-day simple moving average holds at 140,000 points. September 10 formed a doji candle near 143,000 resistance.
The 14-period relative strength index reaches 62 for good momentum. It stays below 70 to avoid overbought signals. MACD shows a bullish cross, though the histogram eases.
Bollinger Bands tighten around the 20-day SMA plus two deviations. This squeeze signals low volatility and a pending shift. Volume lacks strength to confirm gains.
The Global Liquidity Index NDQ yellow line flattens below. It indicates even but stalled fund flows to assets. This limits global backing for Brazilian positions.
The four-hour chart places price over the 20-period EMA at 142,000. Stochastic hits 70, close to overbought. Macro tailwinds aid business, but technical pauses and trade threats demand care.

label: ainvest.com;Regulators and Web3 Innovators Find Common Ground in Historic Talks;https://www.ainvest.com/news/regulators-web3-innovators-find-common-ground-historic-talks-2509/;2025-09-11T07:37:00+00:00
text:
Regulators and Web3 Innovators Find Common Ground in Historic Talks
- Mysten Labs met with SEC's Crypto Task Force in April 2025 to discuss blockchain innovation and regulatory alignment.
- The Sui blockchain developer emphasized compliance needs amid SEC's focus on transparency and investor protection.
- Industry observers view the engagement as a step toward structured crypto regulation balancing innovation and oversight.
- The dialogue reflects broader U.S. government efforts to establish clearer digital asset frameworks through public-private collaboration.
Mysten Labs, a prominent player in the blockchain and decentralized technology space, recently held a meeting with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) Crypto Asset Enforcement Task Force, signaling a growing dialogue between major Web3 firms and regulatory bodies in Washington. The meeting, which took place in early April 2025, focused on the intersection of innovation and compliance within the rapidly evolving crypto landscape. While specific details of the discussions remain undisclosed, industry observers have interpreted the engagement as a positive step toward a more structured regulatory framework that could accommodate technological advancements while protecting investors.
Mysten Labs has been a key participant in the development of the
blockchain, a high-performance, modular platform designed to support a wide range of decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts. The company has attracted significant attention due to its technical innovation and investment from major venture capital firms, including afton CAPITAL and a16z. The firm's recent engagement with the SEC underscores the increasing pressure on crypto companies to align their operations with existing legal and regulatory standards, particularly in the wake of high-profile enforcement actions by the commission.During the meeting, representatives from the SEC emphasized the importance of transparency, investor protection, and market integrity, themes that have become central to the commission’s approach to regulating the crypto industry. The Crypto Task Force has been tasked with addressing enforcement challenges in digital assets, including issues surrounding token offerings, trading platforms, and wallet services. While Mysten Labs has not yet issued a token to the public, the company’s involvement in smart contract development and decentralized infrastructure places it in the broader scope of the SEC's regulatory interest.
The engagement also highlights a broader trend of collaboration between the U.S. government and private sector actors in the crypto space. In recent months, the Department of the Treasury and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) have also issued new guidelines and proposed rule changes aimed at enhancing oversight of digital assets. Mysten’s proactive approach to engaging with regulators is seen as a strategic move to shape the policy environment in favor of innovation while maintaining legal compliance.
Industry analysts have noted that the SEC’s engagement with firms like Mysten Labs could signal a shift in regulatory tone. While the commission has historically taken a firm stance on enforcement, recent dialogues suggest a potential openness to working with companies to establish clearer standards and guidelines. This could lead to a more predictable regulatory environment, which is often cited as a key barrier to mainstream adoption of blockchain and crypto technologies.

Investors Chase Ethereum’s ETF Surge Amid Bullish Crypto Cycle
- Bitcoin's price pattern mirrors 2017's bull cycle, potentially targeting $200,000 if trends persist.
- Ethereum rebounds near $4,433 after 14.1% dip, driven by ETF inflows and institutional adoption.
- Ethereum ETFs like iShares and Fidelity funds saw 113% and 46% asset growth in three months.
- High volatility (beta 4.8) warns of short-term unpredictability despite long-term bullish fundamentals.
Bitcoin,
, and have all shown notable gains in recent market activity, with Bitcoin's price trajectory drawing particular attention for its resemblance to the 2017 bull cycle. Analysts have highlighted several key patterns, including the initial breakout from a bear market, accumulation phases, and a critical green box marking the onset of significant upward momentum. The price movement of suggests it could potentially surpass the $200,000 mark if the current cycle continues as expected.Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, has also experienced a recent resurgence. Following a 14.1% dip from its all-time high set on August 24, Ethereum has regained some ground, rising 1.8% in just two days as of early September. The price is currently hovering near $4,433, just 3.8% below the psychologically important $4,500 threshold. Institutional adoption, the launch of spot ETFs, and increased usage of Ethereum-based stablecoins such as
and Ethena are cited as key drivers of this rally.Ethereum’s ETFs have contributed significantly to the asset’s bullish momentum. Since their launch in July 2024, products such as the iShares Ethereum Trust and the Fidelity Ethereum Fund have attracted substantial inflows. Over the past three months, the iShares Ethereum Trust has seen a 113% increase in assets, while the Fidelity Ethereum Fund has experienced a 46% rise in inflows. These products are enabling a broader range of investors, including high-net-worth individuals, corporations, and retirement accounts, to gain exposure to Ethereum.
The Ethereum network is also benefiting from broader adoption in the blockchain application space. While no single "killer app" has yet emerged, the proliferation of decentralized finance (DeFi) and Web3 projects is building a foundation for long-term value. Additionally, Ethereum-based stablecoins are playing a crucial role in daily transactions, reinforcing the network’s utility and demand.
Despite these bullish indicators, Ethereum remains highly volatile. Its beta value of 4.8 indicates that it is far more susceptible to market swings compared to the S&P 500 index, which has a beta of 1.0. This volatility means that while Ethereum could cross $4,500 in the near term, it may also retrace quickly. Analysts caution that while the long-term outlook is positive, short-term price movements are difficult to predict due to the market’s inherent unpredictability.
