text:
AInvest Newsletter
Daily stocks & crypto headlines, free to your inbox
- Solana's 2025 roadmap combines institutional adoption and Alpenglow upgrades to drive a new bull cycle.
- $1.72B institutional inflows and 7-8% staking yields normalize Solana as a high-yield reserve asset.
- Alpenglow's Votor/Rotor upgrades slash transaction times to 100-150ms and enable real-time financial infrastructure.
- Network efficiency gains and $13B TVL position Solana to capture $100B+ in enterprise blockchain value.
- Regulatory alignment and $5.52B ETF inflow potential suggest $300 price target as institutional adoption accelerates.
The crypto market is entering a pivotal phase where institutional adoption and technical innovation converge to redefine value propositions.
(SOL) stands at the forefront of this shift, with its 2025 roadmap poised to catalyze a new bull cycle. By analyzing the interplay between Solana's treasury backing, transformative network upgrades, and institutional-grade infrastructure, we uncover why this ecosystem is uniquely positioned to outperform in the coming months.Q3 2025 marked a turning point for Solana's institutional narrative. Over $1.72 billion in institutional capital flowed into Solana treasuries, with 13 publicly traded firms collectively holding 1.44% of the total supply[A Strategic Deep Dive into DeFi Development Corp.'s ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990)[1]. This surge is driven by Solana's staking yields, which average 7–8% annually, generating $12–14 million in passive income for institutional portfolios[A Strategic Deep Dive into DeFi Development Corp.'s ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990)[1]. The launch of the REX-Osprey Solana Staking ETF (SSK) in July 2025 further normalized Solana as a reserve asset, attracting $1.2 billion in inflows within 30 days[A Strategic Deep Dive into DeFi Development Corp.'s ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990)[1].
The implications are profound. Institutions are no longer viewing Solana as a speculative asset but as a high-yield, low-risk store of value. With a 99% probability of U.S. spot Solana ETF approval by October 2025, the potential for $5.52 billion in additional inflows within a year underscores this trend[Solana's Path to $300: Historical Patterns, Technical Indicators, ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778)[2]. On-chain data reinforces this narrative: $372 million in whale accumulation and $23 million in exchange withdrawals (60% staked) signal long-term confidence[Solana's Path to $300: Historical Patterns, Technical Indicators, ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778)[2].
While institutional capital fuels demand, Solana's Alpenglow upgrade is the technical catalyst that transforms supply-side dynamics. Approved by 98.27% of Solana's community, this overhaul replaces the existing Proof-of-History (PoH) and TowerBFT consensus mechanisms with Votor and Rotor[Solana's Path to $300: Historical Patterns, Technical Indicators, ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778)[2].
These upgrades are not incremental—they are disruptive. By doubling block space and introducing multiple concurrent proposers, Solana's throughput and scalability will support enterprise-grade applications like supply chain tracking and identity verification[Alpenglow Consensus: Solana's Biggest Protocol Upgrade, [https://blog.quicknode.com/solana-alpenglow-upgrade/]](https://blog.quicknode.com/solana-alpenglow-upgrade/)[3]. The introduction of confidential transfers further enhances privacy, a critical feature for institutional adoption[Alpenglow Consensus: Solana's Biggest Protocol Upgrade, [https://blog.quicknode.com/solana-alpenglow-upgrade/]](https://blog.quicknode.com/solana-alpenglow-upgrade/)[3].
The synergy between Solana's technical prowess and institutional demand creates a self-reinforcing cycle. With 500,000 TPS and $0.00025 gas fees, Solana's DeFi ecosystem has already seen $13 billion in Total Value Locked (TVL)[A Strategic Deep Dive into DeFi Development Corp.'s ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990)[1]. Post-Alpenglow, this figure could surge as enterprises and developers migrate to a platform that combines Web3's decentralization with Web2's efficiency.
Critically, Solana's treasury backing—bolstered by institutional inflows—ensures sustained network security and validator incentives. The $1.72 billion in staked capital across 8.277 million tokens (average yield: 6.86%)[A Strategic Deep Dive into DeFi Development Corp.'s ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604941990)[1] demonstrates that Solana's security model is no longer a vulnerability but a competitive advantage.
Historical patterns and technical indicators suggest Solana's price trajectory is far from capped. The $5.52 billion inflow potential from ETF approval alone could drive demand to levels unseen in 2021[Solana's Path to $300: Historical Patterns, Technical Indicators, ..., [https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778]](https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560604940778)[2]. Meanwhile, Alpenglow's efficiency gains position Solana to capture $100 billion+ in enterprise blockchain value, a market currently underserved by legacy chains.
Bullish momentum is further reinforced by regulatory alignment. The Solana Foundation's engagement with policymakers and the Helix RPS 2.0 project—which decouples read/write layers—address scalability concerns[Alpenglow Consensus: Solana's Biggest Protocol Upgrade, [https://blog.quicknode.com/solana-alpenglow-upgrade/]](https://blog.quicknode.com/solana-alpenglow-upgrade/)[3]. As institutional adoption accelerates and network efficiency outpaces competitors, Solana's price could mirror Bitcoin's 2024 rally, with $300 becoming a realistic target.
Solana's 2025 roadmap is a masterclass in aligning technical innovation with institutional demand. The Alpenglow upgrade eliminates scalability bottlenecks, while treasury backing and staking yields create a flywheel of value accrual. As the line between traditional finance and decentralized infrastructure blurs, Solana is not just a crypto asset—it's a foundational layer for the next era of finance. For investors, the question isn't whether Solana will rise, but how quickly it will outpace the market.

label: dailytimesleader.com;Telekom Srbija Expands and Extends Partnership with SES | User | dailytimesleader.com;http://business.dailytimesleader.com/dailytimesleader/article/bizwire-2025-9-11-telekom-srbija-expands-and-extends-partnership-with-ses;2025-09-11T07:52:00+00:00
text:
Leading Balkan DTH provider adds capacity to consolidate its m:Sat TV platform at 23.5 degrees East and serve more customers across the region
SES announced today the expansion of its partnership with Telekom Srbija , adding two additional transponders and extending its capacity agreements through 2032. Telekom Srbija will use the added capacity to consolidate its m:Sat TV platform at the 23.5 degrees East orbital position to grow its direct-to-home (DTH) television base across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and North Macedonia. The two companies first joined forces in 2011, with expanded renewals in 2020 and 2024.
Under the new agreement, SES will continue to provide capacity on multiple transponders to support a broad lineup of SD and HD channels throughout the region, alongside uplink and backup services and redundant fiber connectivity for the platform. Satellite remains the infrastructure of choice of when it comes to high-quality content broadcasting in the region, underscoring its key value proposition as a reliable and cost-effective video delivery to large audiences.
“The continued expansion of our partnership with SES strengthens our ability to deliver premium television experiences to households across the region,” said Vladimir Lucic, CEO at Telekom Srbija. “With the additional capacity and SES’s proven service reliability, we can scale our DTH offering with confidence and meet the rising demand for high-quality entertainment.”
“Telekom Srbija has been a valued partner for well over a decade, and this long-term extension underscores our shared commitment to bringing high-quality video to viewers across the Western Balkans,” said Deepak Mathur, President Media Vertical at SES. “By adding capacity at 23.5 degrees East, we’re giving Telekom Srbija the ability to consolidate and grow its subscriber base and channel lineup while maintaining the reliability and service excellence their customers expect.”

Telekom Serbia occupies the leading position in the Serbian telecommunications market, providing a unique and integrated customer experience. Operating under the mts brand in Serbia, the company offers mobile and fixed telephony, TV, and internet services. By introducing new services and implementing state-of-the-art technologies, the company strives to facilitate global connectivity and to enrich people’s lives by creating conditions for outstanding communication.
Owing to continuous investments in the development and modernization of telecommunications infrastructure, network and services, the company can successfully respond to various challenges, customer demands and expectations. Telekom Serbia Group boasts a versatile portfolio of telecommunication services and direct operations in several countries in the region, serving more than 10 million customers while maintaining a global presence by selling television services worldwide.
Over the last decade, the company has been building its capacities in the production and distribution of exclusive TV series, feature films and sports content. Telekom Srbija has thus supplemented its portfolio of top services with the production of high-quality documentary and featured programmes, delivered across all its multimedia platforms and partners’ TV networks, presenting relevant and attractive content for further distribution worldwide.

Peru’s 12-month economic expectations rose from 58.3 points in July to 60.1 points in August, according to the latest Macroeconomic Expectations Survey, the

label: gulfnews.com;Saudi fashion brand Jamjoom prices IPO at SAR145 a share, raises SAR346 million;https://gulfnews.com/business/markets/saudi-fashion-brand-jamjoom-prices-ipo-at-sar145-a-share-raises-sar346-million-1.500265283;2025-09-11T07:37:00+00:00
text:
IPO attracted strong interest from investors, with order book totaling SAR1.557 billion
Dubai: Jamjoom Fashion Trading Company, a leading Saudi apparel and lifestyle group behind brands including Nayomi and Mihyar, has completed its initial public offering (IPO), pricing shares at SAR145 each, the top end of its previously announced range of SAR140–145.
The offering, which sold 2,384,340 shares, represents 30% of the company’s capital and raises SAR 346 million ($92 million). At this price, Jamjoom Fashion’s market capitalization at listing is estimated at SAR1.15 billion ($307 million).
The IPO attracted strong interest from qualified investors, with the order book oversubscribed 4.5 times, totaling SAR 1.557 billion.
Kamal Osman Jamjoom, Founder and Chairman, highlighted the strong demand as a vote of confidence in Saudi homegrown brands. He said the offering reflects investor confidence in the company’s growth model, which combines online and physical retail channels, and underscores the potential of the Kingdom’s retail sector.
Final offer price: SAR145 per share.
Total offering size: SAR346 million ($92 million).
Listing venue: Parallel Market (Nomu) of the Saudi Exchange.
Ownership post-IPO: Selling shareholder Kamal Osman Jamjoom Trading Company will retain 70% of the company’s share capital.
Lock-up period: Selling shareholder subject to a 12-month restriction on selling remaining shares.
Oversubscription: Order book reached 4.5 times the offering size.
The IPO was managed by EFG Hermes KSA, which served as financial advisor and lead manager. A wide network of local investment banks, including Al Rajhi Capital, SNB Capital, Saudi Fransi Capital, Riyad Capital, and others, acted as receiving agents for qualified investors.
The final allocation of shares has been completed, with surplus funds to be refunded to investors by 11 September 2025, without any commissions or deductions from the lead manager or receiving agents.
This IPO marks a milestone for Jamjoom Fashion, reinforcing its position as a key player in the Saudi and GCC retail market while providing investors an opportunity to participate in the growth of homegrown brands with regional expansion ambitions.

label: indiatimes.com;Market eyes festive rally as India-US trade talks spark optimism - The Economic Times;https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/market-eyes-festive-rally-as-india-us-trade-talks-spark-optimism/articleshow/123825482.cms;2025-09-11T07:42:00+00:00
text: Indian markets showed resilience on Wednesday, managing to hold gains despite easing off from intraday highs. The Nifty flirting around the 25,000 mark has investors asking whether this could be the start of a breakout from the narrow trading range seen over recent months.Dipan Mehta, market strategist, weighed in on the potential impact of trade talks in an interview to ET Now. “Yes, if a favourable trade deal is concluded, it will act as a sentiment booster and could be the trigger for markets to break out of the narrow trading range they have been stuck in for months. However, fundamentally it won’t impact a large number of companies. Even when the earlier trade deal came through, only a few listed companies were affected by the tariffs. So, the impact this time as well will be largely sentimental rather than structural.” I do not think it will have much of an impact on the corporate earnings, but right now what the street is really focused on is whether in this particular festive season we will see an improvement in the earnings growth rate. The reason the market is pinned down is because earnings growth is not coming through and now many measures have been taken to boost earnings growth. We need to now finally see whether the earnings actually go up and that only can take the markets higher. Of course, the market is not correcting because of the huge surge of liquidity coming in from retail investors, but how long that will also last is questionable. Most importantly the eye has to be on earnings growth,” he added.The auto sector, expected to be a major beneficiary of the GST reset, has seen mixed movements. Despite a recent rally, the sector slipped today, prompting questions about re-entry opportunities.“No, I still believe that we should be overweight auto companies and with usual disclosure that we and our clients are interested, invested. Entry level companies like Hero MotoCorp certainly are far more interesting than some of the peer group companies where valuations also are reasonable and with rural demand expected to pick up, that is one company which can benefit. So, the two-wheeler Hero MotoCorp and Eicher Motors, of course, have been all-time favourites of us. These are two companies to consider.And on the four-wheeler side, very-very positive on M&M, again disclosure required over here. So, investors should be overweight in the auto industry. Definitely we are expecting a nice improvement in the volumes across the board and even if you have shares in other companies, whether it is Bajaj Auto or TVS or Maruti, the entire sector should do pretty well over the next few quarters or so. Raw material costs are benign, and the auto industry, all of them, will take this GST cut opportunity and put in everything that is required to boost their sales. Who knows, if they get volumes which are in double digit growth rate, then that could be a big fillip to the bottom line of these companies,” he said.With trade optimism and seasonal demand playing a key role, analysts believe the coming weeks could set the tone for market direction and sectoral performance, especially for auto stocks. Investors will be keeping a close watch on corporate earnings and volume growth as the festive season unfolds.

label: ppioneer.com;Tax relief for hardworking Americans;https://www.ppioneer.com/articles/tax-relief-for-hardworking-americans/;2025-09-10T22:17:00+00:00
text:
Next year, working families in every county in South Dakota will see tax relief thanks to the One Big, Beautiful Bill. And because Republicans worked to make the tax cuts enacted in 2017 permanent, hardworking South Dakota families can be sure that they won’t face a massive tax hike down the road, which means they can spend, invest, and save more of their hard-earned money with more certainty about the future.
In 2017, we lowered tax rates for every income level, doubled the child tax credit, and nearly doubled the standard deduction, among other reforms. This year, Republicans made those reforms permanent. Lower tax rates mean big savings for working families. The higher standard deduction both simplifies the process and lowers your tax burden. Plus, we enacted a new $6,000 bonus deduction for seniors, giving roughly 200,000 South Dakota seniors more breathing room next tax season.
This bill also eliminated taxes on tips and overtime pay. That will bring significant tax savings for millions of workers who earn tips. And folks like first responders, police officers, nurses, and other workers picking up extra shifts and earning overtime pay will now be able to keep more of their hard-earned money, too.
South Dakota small business owners, farmers, and ranchers will also see tax relief because of this bill. They will benefit from lower tax rates and the 199A small business deduction, as well as from investment incentives that make it easier to invest in new equipment and free up cash to invest in their employees and operations. And this bill raises the death tax exemption threshold, which means a lot more family-owned businesses, farms, and ranches won’t have to worry about a big tax bill wiping out what they’ve spent their lives building when they pass their business down to the next generation.
We also included a number of provisions to the tax code that benefit South Dakota families. We further raised the child tax credit and created new investment accounts for children that come with an initial $1,000 from the government. The money that families invest in these accounts can be used down the road for children’s education, to buy their first home, or start a business – to get a running start on their American Dream.
Thanks to this bill, America’s tax code is now permanently oriented toward supporting working families, building up our nation’s economy, and creating jobs here at home. I’m proud that Republicans have delivered permanent tax relief, and I’m eager to see the results begin to play out in South Dakota and across America.

Centurion Accommodation REIT, a spinoff from worker and student housing provider Centurion Corp, is seeking to raise S$771.1 million (US$601 million or RM2.54 billion) through the sale of 876.2 million units at S$0.88 each, according to terms of the deal seen by Bloomberg News . The share sale comes on the heels of a larger US$773 million listing this year of NTT DC REIT, which was the country’s biggest IPO in eight years, according to data compiled by Bloomberg .

label: pakistantoday.com.pk;Private sector lending falls 16.4% in H1 2025, ADR hits 11-year low;https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2025/09/11/private-sector-lending-falls-16-4-in-h1-2025-adr-hits-11-year-low/;2025-09-11T07:40:00+00:00
text:
Pakistan’s banking sector saw a contraction in lending to the private sector during the first half of 2025, as advances fell by over 15%. This sharp decline led to the lowest Advances-to-Deposit Ratio (ADR) in more than a decade, raising concerns about weakening credit for businesses, according to the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) mid-year review.
In the first half of 2025, advances contracted by 16.4%, pushing the ADR down to 35.3%, the lowest level since June 2014. While deposits increased by 17.7%, asset growth was largely driven by investments in government securities, signaling a shift toward low-risk investments and the crowding out of private credit.
This reduction in credit availability reflects weak demand for loans and a cautious approach by banks, which are increasingly prioritizing government securities over extending credit to key industries. The drop in the ADR has raised concerns about the slowing pace of investment, industrial activity, and job creation.
The contraction in private sector lending also contributed to a rise in the gross non-performing loans (NPL) ratio, which increased to 7.4% by June 2025 from 6.3% at the end of 2024, despite a decline in the actual stock of bad loans. Although provisioning levels improved, the uptick in NPLs highlights vulnerabilities in credit growth, particularly for sectors like textiles, energy, and services.
On the earnings front, banks reported steady profitability, benefitting from lower interest expenses following recent policy rate cuts. However, fiscal pressures have led to an increased reliance on banking sector profits to meet government revenue needs, with banks paying 54.5% of their pre-tax profit in taxation, the highest share in recent years.

BC modules at different time periods
The energy yield gain also differs in different irradiance condition. The lower the irradiance, the higher the yield gain of TOPCon over N-type BC, the highest of 9.13% at irradiance if 0-100W/m2 (shown as Figure 4).

BC modules under different irradiance levels
Conclusions
These analysis results revealed that the lower the irradiance the higher the energy yield of TOPCon versus N-type BC to a value higher than that obtained in present study (+3.6%).
The loss mechanism for lower yield of N-type BC was attributed to low bifaciality and poor low irradiance performance due to cell properties (multiple leakage current effects and grid on the back side) . These analyses also revealed that the TOPCon energy yield gain over N-type BC can be increased further to 11.25% and 7.62% in early morning 6am-7am and later afternoon 6pm-7pm respectively.The average energy yield gain of TOPCon over N-type BC module is 8.92% in dusk and dawn. label: ainvest.com;The Meme Coin Mania of 2025: Decoding the Psychology Behind Short-Term Momentum;https://www.ainvest.com/news/meme-coin-mania-2025-decoding-psychology-short-term-momentum-2509/;2025-09-11T07:55:00+00:00
text:

- Meme coins like DOGE and PEPE thrive in 2025, driven by social media trends, influencer hype, and retail FOMO despite lacking utility.
- Platforms like TikTok and X act as de facto market makers, creating viral feedback loops that amplify short-term price surges through community-driven campaigns.
- Regulatory scrutiny intensifies as $6B is lost to scams in H1 2025, while projects add deflationary mechanics to mask speculative nature amid macroeconomic risks.
- 31% of U.S. crypto investors use meme coins as their first entry point, highlighting their cultural impact despite inherent volatility and governance challenges.
In 2025, meme coins have cemented their place as both a cultural phenomenon and a speculative asset class. Tokens like
(DOGE), Pepe (PEPE), and even niche projects like Fartcoin ($FARTCOIN) continue to defy traditional financial logic, driven instead by the whims of social media trends, influencer endorsements, and the collective psychology of retail investors. This article dissects the mechanics of meme coin momentum, the role of viral events, and the risks inherent in a market where sentiment often trumps fundamentals.Meme coins thrive on a unique blend of fear of missing out (FOMO) and herd behavior. According to a report by Seeking Alpha, the meme coin market operates less like a traditional investment arena and more like an entertainment-driven ecosystem, where viral traction and influencer actions dictate price movements*2025 Meme Coin Gold Rush: Late-Stage Entry Strategies*[2]. For instance, Dogecoin's 2021 surge—fueled by Elon Musk's tweets and the
The psychology here is simple: investors are not buying tokens for utility but for the thrill of outpacing the crowd. This is evident in the rise of projects like Arctic Pablo Coin (APC), which, despite lacking tangible use cases, has attracted millions in trading volume through community-driven "shill" campaigns*2025 Meme Coin Gold Rush: Late-Stage Entry Strategies*[2].
Social media platforms have evolved into de facto market makers for meme coins. A 2025 analysis by Coinrule highlights how
AMAs, TikTok challenges, and X-based "pump groups" act as catalysts for short-term price surgesHowever, this momentum is fragile. Negative news, such as a celebrity disavowing a project or a regulatory warning, can trigger abrupt corrections. In May 2025, $FARTCOIN lost 60% of its value overnight after a prominent influencer accused the team of "pump-and-dump" tactics*2025 Meme Coin Gold Rush: Late-Stage Entry Strategies*[2].
While meme coins were once pure jokes, some projects are now integrating deflationary mechanics and utility features to extend their lifespans. For instance, $FARTCOIN introduced a 1% burn fee on transactions in 2025, aiming to reduce supply and theoretically increase scarcity*2025 Meme Coin Gold Rush: Late-Stage Entry Strategies*[2]. Similarly, Pepe (PEPE) partnered with a decentralized gaming platform to create NFT-based rewards for holders*3 Explosive Altcoins to Watch in 2025: Ozak AI, Solana, and Pepe*[3].
These developments suggest a maturation of the meme coin space, but they also raise questions about authenticity. As Bitget notes, "The line between innovation and marketing is increasingly blurred in meme coin ecosystems"*2025 Meme Coin Gold Rush: Late-Stage Entry Strategies*[2]. Investors must scrutinize whether these features add real value or merely serve as PR stunts.
The meme coin market remains a high-risk, high-reward environment. Data from 2025 reveals that over $6 billion was lost to pump-and-dump schemes and liquidity crises in the first half of the year alone*2025 Meme Coin Gold Rush: Late-Stage Entry Strategies*[2]. Regulatory scrutiny is also tightening: the U.S. SEC has launched investigations into several meme coins for alleged market manipulation*How do social media trends influence the value of meme...*[5].
Moreover, the lack of fundamentals means meme coins are inherently vulnerable to macroeconomic shifts. A rise in interest rates or a broader crypto market downturn could see these tokens collapse faster than their more established counterparts.
Meme coins represent a fascinating intersection of finance, culture, and psychology. For 2025, they continue to serve as an on-ramp for new crypto users, with 31% of U.S. investors citing meme coins as their first foray into digital assets*Crypto Adoption Surges in 2025 as Memecoins Drive Growth*[4]. Yet, their speculative nature demands caution. Investors must treat meme coins as high-volatility instruments, not long-term holdings.
As the market evolves, the key to navigating meme coin momentum lies in understanding the social signals that drive it. Whether this trend is a bubble or a new paradigm remains to be seen—but one thing is certain: in the meme coin world, the only constant is change.

label: focustaiwan.tw;Permanent residents, foreign spouses to get NT$10,000 handouts - Focus Taiwan;https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202509110012;2025-09-11T07:42:00+00:00
text:
Taipei, Sept. 11 (CNA) Foreign nationals with permanent residency and foreign residents married to Taiwanese nationals will be eligible for NT$10,000 cash handouts from the government, the Cabinet said Thursday.
At a news briefing in Taipei, National Treasury Administration head Chen Po-cheng (陳柏誠) said the eligibility rules for the planned NT$10,000 (US$329) handouts were largely the same as for the NT$6,000 cash payment distributed in 2023.
● Taiwan's permanent foreign residents eligible for NT$10,000 cash handouts: Premier
As a result, in addition to Taiwanese nationals, foreign permanent residents, foreign spouses of Taiwanese citizens with residence permits, and stateless residents will also qualify for the handouts, Chen said.
The cash handout program is part of a NT$570 billion special package designed to provide financial assistance to businesses and individuals affected by U.S. tariffs on Taiwanese exports, while also strengthening Taiwan's defense infrastructure and Coast Guard.
Following the recent passage of a special act authorizing those measures, the Cabinet on Thursday approved a related special budget bill, which also requires legislative approval before the government can actually access the NT$570 billion in funding.
The cash handouts, expected to be distributed around a month after the proposed special budget is passed by the Legislature and signed into law by President Lai Ching-te (賴清德), are estimated to cost a total of NT$236 billion, according to the Ministry of Finance.
The entire NT$570 billion package will be funded through surplus revenues and borrowing, the ministry added.

Broadcom’s second quarter results were well received by the market, as management highlighted strong demand for AI-related semiconductors and ongoing momentum in its infrastructure software segment. CEO Hock Tan attributed the 22% year-over-year revenue growth primarily to accelerated adoption of custom AI accelerators and robust bookings in both AI semiconductors and VMware. Tan noted, “Demand for custom AI accelerators from our three customers continued to grow as each of them journeys at their own pace towards compute self-sufficiency.” The company also saw improvement in operating margins, supported by product mix and disciplined cost controls.

While we enjoy listening to the management's commentary, our favorite part of earnings calls are the analyst questions. Those are unscripted and can often highlight topics that management teams would rather avoid or topics where the answer is complicated. Here is what has caught our attention.
Our Top 5 Analyst Questions From Broadcom’s Q2 Earnings Call
- Ross Seymore (Deutsche Bank) asked if the acceleration in AI revenue was solely due to the new customer or also stronger demand from existing clients. CEO Hock Tan said both factors contributed, with the fourth customer providing immediate and substantial demand.
- Harlan Sur (JPMorgan) questioned the outlook for non-AI semiconductor recovery and whether recent order trends pointed to a cyclical upturn. Tan replied that while bookings are up year-over-year, recovery is slow and uneven, with broadband showing the most promise.

label: hani.co.kr;KOSPI rallies to record high, up 22.8% since Lee administration took office;https://english.hani.co.kr/arti/english_edition/e_business/1218243.html;2025-09-11T00:00:00+00:00
text:
The KOSPI rewrote history for the first time in four years, hitting a record high on Wednesday. The KOSDAQ hit a yearly high after rising by 0.99% to close at 833.0 points.
The Korea Exchange’s rates on Wednesday showed the KOSPI finishing at 3,314.53, up 54.48 points (1.67%) from the day before. The new high comes just over four years since the index broke the record on July 6, 2021, when it closed at 3,305.21.
The day after Wall Street’s three main indexes closed at record highs on Tuesday (local time), Seoul’s stock market saw the KOSPI begin trading at 3,272.20, up 12.15 points (0.37%), before gradually increasing in growth. It broke the 3,300-point barrier at 9:31 am, leaping up to 3,317.77 at 2:23 pm, breaking the previous intraday high of 3,316.08 recorded on June 25, 2021.
The rally was buoyed by foreign investors, who bought 1.311 trillion won in the securities market and the KOSPI 200 market. Institutional investors also bought 90.29 billion won worth of shares.
Individually, SK Hynix share prices surged 5.56% to 304,000 won, spearheading the rise in the KOSPI index.
The KOSPI, which ended 2024 at 2,399.49, rose to 3,254.47 on July 30, only to remain stagnant for approximately a month following the proposed changes to tax policies announced on Aug. 1, and the South Korean government’s trade deal with the US.
Since Sept. 2, the index has risen for seven straight trading days.
Market analysts attribute this surge to investors’ optimism that the US Federal Reserve will cut interest rates next week, which is predicted to increase liquidity, and the expectation that the Lee Jae Myung administration will relax capital gains tax rules for major shareholders.
The KOSPI has gained 38.1% in 2025, rising 22.8% since the inauguration of the Lee administration following the election on June 3.
Despite foreign investors’ eagerness to buy, the won-dollar exchange rate remained largely stationary, closing the trading day at 1,338.6 won to the dollar, 1.3 won lower than the day before. This can be attributed to the strength of the dollar following Israel’s strike on Doha, Qatar, the day before.

label: newsbreak.com;Novo Nordisk to cut 9,000 jobs in global restructuring - NewsBreak;https://www.newsbreak.com/njbiz-2010983/4226861329499-novo-nordisk-to-cut-9-000-jobs-in-global-restructuring;2025-09-10T14:20:00+00:00
text:
By Kimberly Redmond ,
18 hours ago
The basics:
Novo Nordisk plans to cut roughly 9K jobs globally
Workforce reductions aim to save $1.3B annually by 2026
Layoffs will allow focus on diabetes, obesity growth initiatives
Impact on U.S. headquarters in Plainsboro still unclear
Novo Nordisk is set to lay off roughly 9,000 employees across its global workforce of 78,400 as part of a newly launched restructuring initiative.
In a Sept. 10 press release , the Danish pharmaceutical giant said the transformation plan aims to streamline operations and redirect resources to growth opportunities within diabetes and obesity. Novo Nordisk expects the campaign to generate about $1.3 billion in savings annually by the end of 2026.
The pharma whose portfolio includes blockbuster weight loss drug Wegovy and diabetes shot Ozempic said about 5,000 of the job cuts will occur in its home country.It is not immediately clear what the impact will be at Novo Nordisk’s U.S. headquarters in New Jersey.
"This is a global transformation, and each country, site or region will be impacted differently," a company representative told NJBIZ. "We will not be able to share specific numbers or additional facts about the US until plans are finalised and the appropriate consultations have been carried out in line with local labour laws."
After establishing its presence 43 years ago on Alexander Road in Princeton , the company relocated and consolidated its base to a redeveloped campus on Scudders Mill Road in Plainsboro .
According to Novo Nordisk, affected employees will start receiving layoff communications “over the next few months,” pending local labor negotiations.
The company said it anticipates layoffs across operations, including staff areas and headquarters functions.
Novo Nordisk said it will redirect savings from the workforce reductions to “growth opportunities in diabetes and obesity, including commercial execution initiatives and R&D programs.” It will also explore other ways to “enhance organizational focus, performance culture and speed of decision-making as well as cost efficiencies.”
Necessary evolution
Once the first mover in GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, Novo Nordisk has struggled to maintain market share, particularly in the key U.S. region, amid increased competition from rival Eli Lilly and cheaper compounded weight loss drugs.
A box of Wegovy (semaglutide) injectable prescription medication, a weight-loss drug from Novo Nordisk. - DEPOSIT PHOTOS
In recent years, manufacturing constraints and patient demand created significant early supply constraints for both Wegovy and Ozempic. As a result, the company said it invested $6.5 billion to increase domestic manufacturing capacity of the medications.
Now, the company faces increased competition on two commercial fronts from Eli Lilly’s weight loss drug Zepbound as well as the scores of compounding pharmacies that started producing cheaper, copycat versions of GLP-1 drugs while they were in short supply.
Though compounding of both Novo Nordisk’s and Eli Lilly’s GLP-1 is essentially restricted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration , that hasn’t entirely stopped some compounders.
In a statement, Novo Nordisk said, “The transformation reflects the company’s commitment to meet rising global demand while also competing in a more dynamic and consumer-driven obesity market, as evidenced by the recent slowdown in growth.”
“Over the past years, Novo Nordisk’s rapid scaling has increased organizational complexity and costs. The transformation aims at addressing that complexity, so Novo Nordisk can invest more behind its science, commercial capabilities and manufacturing ramp-up aiming to reach the millions of people who remain untreated,” it said.
Over the past years, Novo Nordisk’s rapid scaling has increased organizational complexity and costs. The transformation aims at addressing that complexity ...
Novo Nordisk statement
Aligning resources
The move comes a little over a month after Novo Nordisk’s executive shakeup. New CEO Maziar Mike Doustdar took the helm in July in the wake of the surprise ouster of Lars Fruergaard Jrgensen. The company attributed the decision to part ways with Jrgensen to market challenges and a drop in its share price in recent months.
Novo Nordisk diabetes drug Ozempic. - PROVIDED BY NOVO NORDISK
Doustdar said in a statement, “As the global leader in obesity and diabetes, Novo Nordisk delivers life-changing products for patients worldwide. But our markets are evolving, particularly in obesity, as it has become more competitive and consumer-driven. Our company must evolve as well.
"This means instilling an increased performance-based culture, deploying our resources ever more effectively, and prioritizing investment where it will have the most impact behind our leading therapy areas.”
He went on to say, “It is always difficult to see talented and valued colleagues go, but we are convinced that this is the right thing to do for the long-term success of Novo Nordisk. We need a shift in our mindset and approach so we can be faster and more agile.
"Our transformation plan is designed to deliver this. By realigning our resources now, we will be able to prioritize investments to drive sustainable growth and future innovation for the millions of patients with chronic diseases globally, particularly in diabetes and obesity.”

text:
(LEAD) Seoul shares set new record high on tech gains, hopes for withdrawal of tax revision proposal
All News16:47 September 11, 2025
(ATTN: ADDS bond yields at bottom, details in 11th para, photo)
SEOUL, Sept. 11 (Yonhap) -- South Korean stocks reached a new record high Thursday, extending their winning streak to an eighth session, driven by tech gains and hopes that President Lee Jae Myung may reverse a controversial capital gains tax hike proposal. The local currency was trading lower against the greenback.
The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) added 29.67 points, or 0.9 percent, to close at 3,344.2. It broke the previous all-time high of 3,314.53 posted the previous day.
Trade volume was moderate at 430.3 million shares worth 14.7 trillion won (US$10.6 billion), with winners slightly outnumbering losers 462 to 403.
Foreigners and institutions were net buyers of local shares, purchasing 300 billion won and 812.3 billion won, respectively, while retail investors dumped 1.1 trillion won for profit taking.
Overnight, the S&P 500 closed 0.3 percent higher and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite inched up 0.03 percent, driven by sharp gains in cloud provider Oracle and AI-related shares, such as Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, closed 0.48 percent lower.
The fresh U.S. producer price data, which showed a decline for the first time in four months, boosted optimism that the Federal Reserve will cut its key rate next week.
Investors' eyes are now on the U.S. consumer price index for August due out on Thursday (U.S. time), which will provide additional clues about the Fed's monetary direction.
The overnight AI rally on Wall Street drove up the KOSPI, which was further boosted by President Lee Jae Myung's press conference marking his first 100 days in office, where he reiterated his plan to foster the growth of Korea's capital markets, said Lee Kyoung-min, an analyst at Daishin Securities.
The president said there is no reason to push forward with his administration's initial plan to lower the capital gains tax threshold for stock investments, which had sparked concerns for local investors.
The analyst also attributed sharp gains in the defense and food sectors to the KOSPI's rise.
In Seoul, market bellwether Samsung Electronics increased 1.1 percent to 73,400 won, while its chipmaking rival SK hynix climbed 0.9 percent to reach an all-time high of 307,000 won.
Leading battery maker LG Energy Solution surged 2.76 percent to 350,000 won, and defense powerhouse Hanwha Aerospace soared 3.93 percent to surpass 1 million won.
Major shipbuilders were also strong, with HD Hyundai Heavy jumping 2.58 percent to 517,000 won, Hanwha Ocean rising 1.72 percent to 112,600 won and HD Korea Shipbuilding advancing 2.05 percent to 423,000 won.
Top automaker Hyundai Motor expanded 1.13 percent to 223,000 won.
Notably, renewable energy companies rallied on President Lee's vow to foster the industry.
SK Oceanplant shot up more than 22 percent to 29,100 won and Doosan Fuel Cell skyrocketed 15.82 percent to 30,750 won.
Food companies were also bullish on the back of the soaring popularity of Korean culture, with instant noodle maker Nongshim escalating 19.17 percent to 488,000 won and its rival Samyang Foods gaining 5.23 percent to 1.6 million won.
But power plant manufacturer Doosan Enerbility dropped 2.56 percent to 61,000 won on the dim prospects of the domestic nuclear power industry, and Korea Electric Power lost 2.97 percent to 37,550 won.
The local currency was quoted at 1,391.8 won against the U.S. dollar at 3:30 p.m., down 5.2 won from the previous session.
Bond prices, which move inversely to yields, closed higher. The yield on three-year Treasurys went down 1.0 basis point to 2.420 percent, while the return on the benchmark five-year government bonds declined 0.9 basis point to 2.557 percent.

label: socialnews.xyz;BiteSpeed Crosses USD 5 Million in ARR, Targets USD 10 Million ARR by Year-End;https://www.socialnews.xyz/2025/09/11/bitespeed-crosses-usd-5-million-in-arr-targets-usd-10-million-arr-by-year-end/;2025-09-11T07:35:00+00:00
text:
Business Wire India
BiteSpeed, an AI-native marketing and support CRM purpose-built for e-commerce brands, announced today that it has surpassed $5 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR), representing a 250% year-on-year growth. The milestone highlights BiteSpeed’s rapid ascent as one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in the global e-commerce technology ecosystem.
Founded in 2019 and backed by leading investors including Peak XV’s Surge (formerly Sequoia Capital India), Whiteboard Capital, and Kunal Shah, BiteSpeed enables e-commerce businesses to personalise their marketing and support interactions across channels like WhatsApp, Email, SMS, Instagram, Voice, and Web Chat from a single AI-powered platform.
Its intelligent AI features allow brands to recover abandoned carts, send personalised order updates, re-engage dormant shoppers, and provide real-time support- all from a unified dashboard. By combining marketing automation with conversational AI, BiteSpeed helps Shopify-first merchants boost conversions and customer lifetime value while reducing operational complexity.
Today, BiteSpeed powers growth for more than 5,000 brands across 50+ countries, including leading brands such as Dot & Key, Bombay Shaving Company, Mokobara, Minimalist, mCaffeine, and Zouk. The company has seen rapid adoption in India and significant traction in international markets, including the UK, the Middle East, South Africa, and Australia.
“Crossing $5 million in ARR shows the trust our customers place in us and the impact BiteSpeed delivers,” said Vinayak Aggarwal, Founder & CEO of BiteSpeed. “As e-commerce brands grow, they need AI tools that turn every interaction into revenue- and that’s exactly what we’re building.”
Building on this momentum, BiteSpeed is rolling out a slate of new features, including AI voice agents and AI-native email marketing to help brands drive more revenue from its platform.
To support this expansion, the company also plans to rapidly scale its team size to over 100 employees by the end of the year. BiteSpeed is hiring for multiple roles across areas like sales, customer success, engineering, growth, and more.
“After carefully building the company focused on fundamentals for the last 5 years, we are now at an inflection point in our journey,” said Vinayak. “With growth being the key focus in this next phase, we’re looking for the right talent to help us shape the future of AI-native e-commerce.”
With its accelerating growth, expanding global footprint, and continuous product innovation, BiteSpeed is cementing its position as the category leader for AI-native CRM in the Shopify ecosystem.

label: devdiscourse.com;IEA Raises Global Oil Supply and Demand Forecasts Amid Uncertain Market Dynamics | Headlines;https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/headlines/3623746-iea-raises-global-oil-supply-and-demand-forecasts-amid-uncertain-market-dynamics;2025-09-11T08:00:00+00:00
text: The International Energy Agency has increased its forecast for global oil supply and demand growth due to OPEC+'s production hike. Amidst this, potential supply challenges arise from new sanctions on Russia and Iran, against a backdrop of higher OPEC+ output and possibly inflated oil inventories. The International Energy Agency (IEA) has adjusted its expectations for global oil supply and demand growth upwards, spurred by the recent decision from OPEC+ to boost production. This revision signals a complex market landscape shaped by persistent deliveries in advanced economies. OPEC+ production increases are juxtaposed with potential supply disruptions from new sanctions imposed on Russia and Iran. These factors create a multifaceted narrative for oil markets, driving divergent forces that could impact supply balances globally. The IEA's monthly oil market report suggests that the sector could face compounded pressure from heightened production levels and the risk of surplus inventory, creating uncertainty for stakeholders across the energy domain.

THG, which owns brands like Myprotein, Cult Beauty and Glossybox, saw first-half sales across the business fall 2.6% at constant currencies (CCY), as a 3.1% increase in the Nutrition division was offset by a 5.9% decline in the larger Beauty division.
However, the company reported a turnaround in the second quarter, with CCY sales growing by 0.9% after dropping 6.1% in the first quarter.

"I'm really pleased at how THG has gained momentum throughout the first half and into Q3. A slower start to the year in Beauty, alongside record whey prices in Nutrition, initially held back performance, but we saw clear improvement in Q2, in particular supported by Myprotein offline retail and licensing sales," said chief executive Matthew Moulding.
"Our momentum is positive and Q3 will be our strongest trading period of the year so far, underpinning our confidence in the outlook."
Results for the six months to 30 June, which were well flagged in recent trading updates, showed revenues of £783.4m, down 7.6% on last year on a reported basis, while adjusted EBITDA sank 35.3% to £24m.

text: Of the two inflation reports out this week, PPI is the lesser of the two in terms of importance, but it came in far enough below forecasts to prompt some bond buying to start the day. PPI is a complex report relative to CPI, but one of the simplest takeaways from today's data is that wholesalers drastically decreased the extent to which they were passing along higher costs via margins. Another simple takeaway is that a lot of today's apparent downward surge had to do with the previous report's big upward surge. Even after revisions, last month's PPI rose at 0.7%, thus creating a low bar for today's data to come in soft. Looked at another way, the average monthly PPI over the past two months would still be 0.3% (or 3.6% annually) when taking the average of the super hot July and super cool August numbers.

label: cxotoday.com;AI at the Frontline: Reshaping Cybersecurity with Smarter Threat Detection and Response;https://cxotoday.com/interviews/ai-at-the-frontline-reshaping-cybersecurity-with-smarter-threat-detection-and-response/;2025-09-11T07:54:00+00:00
text:
CXOToday has engaged in an exclusive interview with Umashankar Lakshmipathy, EVP and Co-head of CIS and CyberSecurity, Infosys.
How are AI and ML reshaping the cybersecurity landscape today, particularly in threat detection and incident response? Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates improved business outcomes and is increasingly regarded as a crucial component of any enterprise’s ecosystem. In the coming years, this momentum will continue to grow, and the importance of AI will become even more pronounced. Notably, AI and ML are transforming the cybersecurity landscape by enabling faster and more effective threat detection and response. This is vital, as a rapidly evolving and complex threat environment demands continuous strengthening of security postures and robust defenses against sophisticated cyberattacks such as ransomware and phishing.
Traditional threat detection methods, such as signature-based pattern matching, have been effective for identifying known threats. However, they fall short in detecting new or zero-day threats, including those augmented by AI. With its ability to analyze large volumes of data swiftly, infer patterns, and generate predictive insights, AI and ML enable real-time threat detection, significantly reducing the window of opportunity for attackers to exploit new vulnerabilities. Furthermore, AI and ML enhance threat intelligence by rapidly analyzing and correlating data from diverse sources to identify emerging threat patterns and contextualize risks – allowing proactive hunting of threats across the enterprise landscape.
Examples of how AI and ML enhance threat detection and incident response include:
Real-time anomaly and threat pattern detection: AI and ML-powered controls continuously monitor data and logs from various sources – such as network traffic, system logs, and access logs – to identify deviations from established baselines. Automated incident response: Autonomous security operations, augmented by AI with agentic capabilities, leverage ML, contextual reasoning, and real-time adaptation to automatically initiate response actions. This includes orchestrating automated threat containment workflows and reducing analyst workload. Such AI agents can contextually enrich alerts and triage them more effectively using human-like cognitive reasoning. Prioritized risk remediation: AI and ML algorithms enable the contextualization and prioritization of threats, focusing security efforts on the most critical risks. They process unstructured data – such as dark web intelligence and open-source intelligence feeds – at scale to proactively detect threats, assess risks within the enterprise context, and dynamically prioritize remediation efforts without relying solely on preprogrammed rules. By harnessing AI and ML, enterprises can maintain a strong security posture – enhancing threat detection, automating incident response, and orchestrating security workflows – while minimizing disruptions in an increasingly fast-paced, AI-augmented enterprise ecosystem.
However, it is also well established that adversarial use of AI is rapidly expanding attack surfaces and enabling adversaries to accelerate cyberattack methodologies. Threat actors are exploiting techniques such as Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) to manipulate ML models relied upon for security. Through such manipulation, attackers can undermine the effectiveness of AI-driven controls or even trigger fully autonomous cyberattacks. This presents a significant concern, as the impact of AI and ML on cybersecurity will deepen with ongoing technological evolution. Enterprises must proactively mitigate risks associated with adversarial AI and ML, ensuring their models are designed with principles of security by design and responsible AI adoption – maintaining vigilance to stay ahead of malicious adversaries.
The industry faces a crunch at the intersection of data science and cybersecurity. What makes this talent so scarce, and what skills will define the next generation of “multidisciplinary cyber professional”? The rapid growth in adoption of AI-enabled digital technologies, across industry segments and geographies, require availability of skilled and experienced cybersecurity professionals to protect the enterprise landscape from emerging cyber threats. This has, undoubtedly, increased pressure on the talent supply chain for the availability of skilled cybersecurity professionals who can architect and design the next-generation of AI-powered cyber defenses, ensuring stronger security posture of enterprises in the digital world. The skills required to develop such security controls are multidisciplinary and complex – spanning cybersecurity domains such as identity security, cloud security, and network security, along with expertise in machine learning, data science, deep learning, generative AI, agentic AI, and more. These skills are essential for effective threat detection, autonomous incident response, and robust protection against expanding attack surfaces. However, fulfilling the rising demand for cybersecurity talent faces several challenges, including the lack of well-defined career paths, high costs associated with training and certifications, and concerns about burnout within cybersecurity roles. According to the Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2025 by the World Economic Forum, there is an estimated global shortage of over 4 million cybersecurity professionals.
To address this talent mismatch, enterprises can adopt several measures:
Invest in ongoing training and certification programs to keep cybersecurity professionals updated with emerging technologies, AI security tools, and zero-trust security principles, thereby strengthening the security posture of digital enterprises. Develop clear organizational career development and enablement roadmaps tailored to cybersecurity roles, providing visibility and pathways for career advancement within the field. Establish forums for community participation, knowledge sharing, and best practice exchange among cybersecurity professionals, fostering a sustainable talent development model across enterprises and industry segments. Focus on building AI-enabled cybersecurity skills across all levels of experience within the organization. This approach nurtures multidisciplinary cybersecurity expertise throughout professionals’ careers, helping to moderate the demand for niche skills and ensuring a steady pipeline of capable talent. Leverage AI technologies – such as co-pilots and agentic AI – to amplify cybersecurity capabilities, reduce alert fatigue, and facilitate autonomous incident remediation. This enables cybersecurity professionals to focus on complex areas requiring human judgment and governance, while AI tools assist with data analysis and incident response based on insights from various data sources.
How is Infosys approaching reskilling and recruitment to bridge the talent gap in cybersecurity? Infosys offers diverse training programs, including partnerships with leading academic institutions (e.g., Purdue University), to help employees develop competencies and skills in AI, cybersecurity fundamentals, and related adjacent areas such as Python, data science, and BI reporting. Our training and enablement processes focus on building skills across all employee levels – from early-career professionals to senior executives – in both technological and functional domains of cybersecurity.
For online learning, Infosys has developed the LEX digital platform, which enables anytime access to curated learning paths for upskilling and continuous learning in cybersecurity, AI, and digital technologies. Additionally, we provide access to reputable online platforms like O’Reilly and Cybrary, offering self-paced courses, e-books, and hands-on labs to deepen expertise in cybersecurity tools and practices.
Our strategic alliances with industry leaders such as Zscaler, Cisco, Microsoft, CrowdStrike, and others give employees access to product-specific training and certification portals. This ensures our cybersecurity capabilities remain robust and ready to address emerging and lethal cyber threats. A well-structured learning program has been instrumental in continuously enhancing employees’ foundational and advanced cybersecurity skills through a blend of external educators, partner product vendors, and internal trainers.
Regarding talent acquisition, Infosys employs a comprehensive strategy that includes campus hiring with structured training and mentorship programs, reskilling and cross-skilling professionals from adjacent domains, and specialized lateral hiring initiatives. This approach involves rigorous skill assessments and behavioral evaluations focused on communication, leadership, and customer-centricity – ensuring that new hires are a strong technological and cultural fit within Infosys’s cybersecurity ecosystem.
By leveraging comprehensive training programs, strategic industry collaborations, and targeted talent acquisition initiatives, Infosys is committed to cultivating a resilient, skilled cybersecurity workforce capable of safeguarding digital assets and driving innovation in an ever-evolving cyber landscape.
What are the opportunities and risks in relying on AI-driven cyber defense? AI-driven cyber defense leverages artificial intelligence, primarily through machine learning, to significantly accelerate and automate capabilities for protection, detection, triaging, and response to cyber threats. However, while offering transformative opportunities, AI also introduces new and complex risks. It can be weaponized, leading to more advanced and covert cyberattacks. Therefore, the dual nature of AI – as both a transformative technology and a potential adversarial tool – must be carefully managed to ensure its effective use in augmenting future cybersecurity solutions.
Below are some of the key opportunities and risks associated with reliance on AI-driven cyber defense:
Key Opportunities with AI in Cybersecurity
Enhanced Cyber Resilience: AI significantly improves an enterprise’s security posture by enabling rapid analysis of vast amounts of event data, identifying patterns to detect anomalies, predicting whether an event is benign or malicious, and prescribing actions to proactively deter and respond to threats. Leveraging AI in cyber defense amplifies the capabilities of human security analysts and facilitates autonomous, real-time responses across complex, distributed infrastructures, thereby strengthening overall cyber resilience. Advanced Threat Detection: AI excels at identifying sophisticated attacks such as polymorphic malware, fileless attacks, and living-off-the-land techniques – threat patterns that are difficult to detect with traditional signature-based controls. AI and machine learning models can detect deviations and behavioral outliers, enabling security analysts to proactively investigate and mitigate potential breaches. Proactive Vulnerability Identification: AI-powered security controls can analyze and correlate code, configurations, and architecture to identify potential misconfigurations and vulnerabilities. Through this correlation, security teams gain visibility into the blast radius of misconfigurations, contextualized exploitability analyses, and prioritized focus areas for remediation. Supporting Zero-Trust Security Models: AI-driven cyber defense enhances a robust and responsive security posture by enabling a dynamic zero-trust framework. Continuous risk and trust evaluation, adaptive access controls, attack trajectory prediction, threat pattern analysis, and self-healing networks within zero-trust architectures enable more sophisticated and resilient defenses in ever-evolving threat landscapes. Cost Efficiency: Although initial implementation costs can be high, AI can reduce long-term operational expenses by automating labor-intensive tasks and improving detection accuracy, thereby minimizing the financial impact of successful breaches Risks Associated with Leveraging AI in Cybersecurity
Adversarial AI Attacks: While AI capabilities enhance cyber defense, adversaries can weaponize these technologies to exploit expanding attack surfaces. Attackers are rapidly developing techniques to poison AI training data, evade detection models, and exploit algorithmic vulnerabilities. This creates a continuous race where security defenders must constantly update their AI systems to counter increasingly sophisticated AI-driven cyberattacks. For example, the use of AI-generated deepfakes in advanced phishing and social engineering campaigns, or the development of malware that autonomously adapts to bypass zero-trust security measures. Misplaced Confidence and Over-Reliance: Enterprises may become overly dependent on autonomous and automated AI systems, potentially reducing human oversight and creating blind spots. High confidence scores from AI models do not guarantee accuracy, and analysts might stop scrutinizing automated decisions. For instance, security teams overly reliant on AI to identify attack patterns may overlook novel or complex threats that the models are not trained to recognize. Model Drift and Bias: Over time, the accuracy of AI models can degrade as network environments evolve, leading to increased false positives or missed threats. Additionally, biases present in training data can result in discriminatory outcomes or blind spots for certain attack types or user groups, compromising overall security effectiveness. Explainability Challenges: Advanced AI models, such as deep learning systems, often operate as “black boxes,” making it difficult for analysts to understand how specific decisions are made. This lack of transparency complicates incident investigations, hampers accountability, and raises challenges in establishing auditability. Ensuring explainable AI is essential for building trust and maintaining compliance with regulatory standards. Data Privacy and Governance: AI systems require access to large volumes of sensitive data, posing privacy risks and potential regulatory compliance issues. Poor data governance can lead to model contamination or unauthorized data exposure. Therefore, organizations must implement well-defined policies aligned with relevant legal and regulatory frameworks to ensure responsible AI deployment and governance.
How are AI-powered, platform-led solutions redefining enterprise security models? In what ways do these solutions augment the work of human cyber professionals? The advent of AI-powered, platform-led solutions are transforming enterprise security from reactive, siloed approaches to proactive, adaptive and integrated defense ecosystems. Autonomous agentic AI based cybersecurity solution represents a significant evolution in strengthening defenses and amplifying human potential, with the ability to quickly analyze and respond to cyber incidents. In our view, AI-powered platforms are poised to redefine enterprise security and empower cybersecurity teams across three key areas: Posture, Protection, and Prevention.
Observability and Posture Management: Traditional security stacks comprise point products – such as SIEM, EDR, firewalls, vulnerability scanners, etc. – that operate in silos and require manual correlation of event data. Next-generation AI-driven cybersecurity platforms are built on an integrated data fabric that ingests telemetry from endpoints, networks, cloud workloads, identity systems, and threat intelligence feeds. This enables cross-domain collaboration, comprehensive observability, and the establishment of a unified risk posture. Continuous Adaptive Protection at Scale: Agentic AI-based cybersecurity platforms empower enterprises to shift from reactive to proactive defense. AI agents augment human analysts by providing meaningful, correlated data from multiple heterogeneous sources across the entire enterprise landscape. These AI-powered platforms enhance security analysts’ capabilities by reducing false positives and supporting faster, more informed decision-making through quick analysis of event data. Strategic Business Enablement: Implementing AI-driven, platform-led security yields measurable benefits such as improved Mean Time to Detection (MTTD), reduced Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), and scalable operations through a consolidated platform. Infosys envisions enterprise security as a collaborative ecosystem of cybersecurity services delivered as software. AI platforms will assist less experienced analysts in operating at higher levels by providing guided workflows, contextual information, and automated threat analysis. This approach is vital given the persistent cybersecurity talent shortage. Additionally, AI-powered platforms will deliver risk assessments, attack attribution analysis, and recommended remediation steps. However, humans will retain control over critical decisions, especially those involving business impact or regulatory compliance.
Can you share examples where Infosys’ blend of AI-led tools and skilled professionals has strengthened a client’s cyber resilience? Infosys Cybersecurity helps organizations reimagine their cybersecurity strategies, making them more resilient against disruptions and uncertainties caused by cyber threats. As AI adoption continues to grow, we develop cyber-resilient businesses by implementing solutions that are secure by design, capable of quickly scaling to meet evolving security demands, and prepared to safeguard the future amidst rapidly emerging technological standards and innovations.
With the structural integration of Cyber Resiliency at the core of the enterprise ecosystem, our solutions empower organizations to anticipate threats more quickly, ensure comprehensive protection, and perform precise point-in-time recovery – ultimately minimizing downtime.
Through our AI-powered Cyber Next platform, we empower enterprises to accelerate the consolidation, convergence, and unification of essential cybersecurity capabilities. For several global enterprise customers onboarded to the Infosys Cyber Next platform, we have delivered managed security services through our nine global Cyber Defence Centers (CDCs). Across these CDCs, our cybersecurity analysts continuously monitor, detect, and strengthen cyber defenses by leveraging AI-powered controls, effectively protecting against expanding attack surfaces and emerging adversarial threats. Through early investments, in-depth applied research in cybersecurity, and highly trained teams, Infosys Cybersecurity has accelerated its generative journey by developing and deploying the Generative AI Cyber Advisor. This innovative solution aims to bridge the skill gap, reduce alert fatigue, and seamlessly integrate digital workers into cyber defense operations.
For example, for a metallurgical products organization in US, we deployed an autonomous, agentic AI solution that delivers security incident investigation, triage, and response services as software. This solution achieved a threefold reduction in Mean Time to Identify (MTTI) and autonomously resolved over 90% of false positive alerts. It enabled cybersecurity analysts to concentrate on critical issues while reducing distractions caused by events from multiple sources by 83%.
Additionally, this solution incorporated responsible AI guardrails, accelerated AI adoption for cyber defense against industrialized threat actors, and enhanced operational efficiency to address cybersecurity skill gaps. Ultimately, it transformed cybersecurity into a strategic business enabler for the customer.

label: kyodonews.net;Tokyo stocks close at record highs for 2nd straight day;https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/60845;2025-09-11T07:50:00+00:00
text:
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed at all-time highs for a second straight trading day on Thursday as heavyweight technology shares drew buying amid hopes for growth on the back of artificial intelligence demand.
The 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average gained 534.83 points, or 1.22 percent, from Wednesday to 44,372.50, while the broader Topix index finished 6.79 points, or 0.22 percent, higher at 3,147.76, both record closes.
On the top-tier Prime Market, the main gainers were information and communication, nonferrous metal and mining issues.
The U.S. dollar mostly moved narrowly in the lower 147 yen range in Tokyo for most of the day due to few new trading incentives. Investors were awaiting the release of U.S. consumer price index data for August later in the day, dealers said.
Active buying of tech stocks was triggered by record closes of both the U.S. Nasdaq and S&P 500 indexes overnight, boosted by a 36 percent surge in U.S. software company Oracle on its upbeat business outlook, brokers said.
However, some investors were cautious over chasing the upside as they see the recent record closes as a sign of the Tokyo stock market being overheated, broker said.
Among tech issues, semiconductor-related issues and AI-related stocks, such as SoftBank Group and Advantest rose sharply in particular. SoftBank Group soared 10 percent to 17,905 yen, while Advantest ended up 4.4 percent to 13,700 yen.
Meanwhile, expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will cut interest rates grew stronger as a lower-than-expected U.S. producer price index for August released on Wednesday indicated slowing inflation.
"The market is factoring in the scenario of rate cuts up to three times within this year amid growing expectations," said Masahiro Ichikawa, chief market strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management Co.
"Technology shares were being bought on (expectation for) lower U.S. interest rates and the view that a slowdown in the world's largest economy can be avoided" helped by rate cuts, Ichikawa added.

label: blueprint.ng;National social register cornerstone for inclusive social protection - NSIPA;https://blueprint.ng/national-social-register-cornerstone-for-inclusive-social-protection-nsipa/;2025-09-11T05:11:00+00:00
text:
The national coordinator, National Social Investment Programme Agency (NSIPA), Assoc. Prof. Badamasi Lawal, has urged stakeholders to deepen support for the National Social Register (NSR), describing it as the foundational tool for delivering inclusive social protection in Nigeria.
A press statement issued by the head Information and Public Relations of NSIPA, Attari M. Hope, Tuesday, said Badamasi Lawal made the call in his opening remarks at a one-day stakeholder engagement meeting organised by the National Social Safety-Nets Coordinating Office (NASSCO).
The event was held at Eko Hotel and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos under the theme: “Advancing Social Protection through the National Social Register (NSR).”
Lawal emphasised that the NSR is more than a database; it is a living, dynamic national asset that enables evidence-based planning, strategic targeting and effective service delivery ensuring that poor and vulnerable Nigerians are included in government interventions.
He said NSIPA’s mandate to coordinate, implement and monitor national social investment programmes is aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises education, health and social protection.
Lawal urged stakeholders to treat the NSR as a continuously updated, secured and institutionalised system, and called for renewed collaboration to place people at the center of social protection strategies so that every Nigerian can enjoy dignity, opportunity and hope.
In her welcome address, the national programme manager of NASSCO, Dr. Funmi Olotu, said “under the Tinubu Renewed Hope Agenda, a bold step has been taken: every social intervention must pass through the National Social Register to ensure transparency, accountability and fairness in support for Nigerians.
“Today the National Social Register covers more than 19 million households and over 70 million individuals, making it one of the largest social protection databases in the world,” she said.

The steam boiler market, valued at USD 15.2 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 25.4 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of 5.3%, demonstrates a balanced progression supported by a structured cost and value chain framework. The cost structure of this market is shaped primarily by raw materials such as steel, alloys, pressure vessels, and combustion equipment, which account for a significant share of production expenditure. Fabrication, welding, and quality testing further add to capital intensity, making manufacturing costs a critical determinant of pricing strategies.
Energy and operational efficiency improvements play a key role in value creation, as boiler designs increasingly incorporate advanced combustion systems and automated controls. Supply chain dynamics rely on component suppliers, system integrators, and technology providers who collectively influence lead times and overall cost competitiveness. Distribution is managed through both direct sales channels and industrial solution providers, which add service value including installation, maintenance, and after-sales support.
From a value-chain perspective, equipment manufacturers capture the largest share, while service providers enhance recurring revenue streams through retrofitting and energy optimization solutions. Regulatory compliance costs also affect margins, as emission standards demand continuous R&D investments.

---|---|
